data.title: We made Postgres writes faster, but it broke replication
data.author: philippemnoel
data.article_summary:
文章讲述了在优化Postgres写入速度时遇到的问题及其解决方案。为了提升写入吞吐量，团队在Postgres搜索扩展**pg_search**中使用了**LSM树**（Log-Structured Merge Tree），这种数据结构对写入进行了优化，显著提高了写入性能。然而，这却破坏了Postgres的复制机制，尤其是物理复制。

Postgres通过**WAL日志传输**保证物理一致性，但LSM树的复杂性使得这种机制不足以维持复制安全。物理一致性保证副本数据结构有效，但未必逻辑一致。为了实现逻辑一致性，团队利用了**hot_standby_feedback**设置，并确保在事务处理过程中保持原子性。最终，文章深入探讨了LSM树的结构、复制安全的意义以及如何解决复制问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术深度的内容需求及其实现细节的讨论，特别是关于WAL（Write-Ahead Log）传输、Postgres的VACUUM机制以及替代技术方案（如Elasticsearch和OpenSearch）的选择。

不同观点：
• [timetoogo] 支持发布更多无赘述的技术深度内容，认为HN（Hacker News）需要更多类似内容。
• [kikimora] 同样支持发布更多深度内容，但对WAL传输与内存锁之间的关系感到困惑。具体讨论了WAL的单线程读取与多线程应用问题，并质疑了在块级别上进行原子操作的必要性。此外，还对Postgres的VACUUM机制在主从复制中的问题进行了分析，提出是否应使用自定义存储引擎来解决与Postgres的冲突。
• [otterley] 质疑为何不直接使用现有的OpenSearch或Elasticsearch，认为在已有工具能解决问题的情况下，不应重复造轮子，暗示这种做法可能是不必要的复杂化。

补充讨论：
• [truetraveller] 对文章中提到的图表制作方式表示好奇，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否需要开发自定义解决方案（如自定义存储引擎）来解决Postgres中的问题，还是应尽量利用现有工具（如Elasticsearch、OpenSearch）。[kikimora] 认为自定义存储引擎可能更合适，而[otterley] 则倾向于使用现有的成熟工具以避免不必要的复杂性。

总结：讨论围绕技术内容的需求、WAL的实现细节、Postgres的VACUUM机制及替代技术方案的可行性展开，各方对技术实现的优劣及是否应使用现有工具存在不同见解。

44633933.article_content:
Previous Post
Next Post
We Made Postgres Writes Faster, but it Broke Replication
+2
By Stu Hood, Ming Ying, Mathew Pregasen, and Olive Ratliff on June 30, 2025
When we built
pg_search
, the Postgres extension for search and analytics, write throughput was a priority. To be an effective alternative to Elasticsearch we needed to support high ingest workloads in real time.
This is because many Elasticsearch use cases — like real-time dashboards, e-commerce search, and recommendation systems — involve continuous writes that must be indexed and made searchable immediately.
In a vanilla Postgres implementation, full-text search is backed by a
B-tree
or
GIN
(Generalized Inverted Index) structure. These indexes are good for relatively fast lookups, but they aren’t so fast for writes.
We opted for a data structure optimized for writes: a
Log-Structured Merge (
LSM
) tree
. That was great for write throughput, but it broke Postgres replication! Specifically, it broke physical replication, one of the two mechanisms that allow Postgres to replicate data from a primary node across one or more read replicas.
The other mode is logical replication, which sends individual row changes to replicas instead of copying the database byte-for-byte.
It turned out that Postgres's out-of-the-box support for physical replication, built on Write-Ahead Log (WAL) shipping, isn't quite enough for an advanced data structure like an LSM tree to be replication-safe. We were surprised to learn this, so we decided to write up our experience and describe how we fixed the problem.
In this post, we'll do a deep dive into:
What is an LSM tree?
What it means for an LSM tree to be replication-safe
How Postgres' WAL shipping guarantees physical consistency
Why atomic logging was necessary for logical consistency
How we leveraged a little-known but powerful Postgres setting called
hot_standby_feedback
What is an LSM Tree?
A Log-Structured Merge Tree (LSM tree) is a write-optimized data structure commonly used in systems like RocksDB and Cassandra.
The core idea behind an LSM tree is to turn random writes into sequential ones. Incoming writes are first stored in an in-memory buffer called a memtable, which is fast to update. Once the memtable fills up, it is flushed to disk as a sorted, immutable segment file (often called an SSTable).
These segment files are organized by size into layers or levels. Newer data is written to the topmost layer. Over time, data is gradually pushed down into lower levels through a process called compaction, where data from smaller segments is
merged, deduplicated, and rewritten into larger segments.
What Do We Mean by Replication Safety?
A reliable distributed datastore (one which guarantees “replication safety”) must demonstrate both
physical
and
logical
consistency
1
2
across database replicas.
Physical consistency
means the replica contains structurally valid data — each page or block on disk is well-formed and corresponds to a state that did exist on the primary at some point.
Logical consistency
ensures that the data on the replica reflects a coherent and stable view of the database, something that could have been seen by a transaction on the primary.
A physically consistent state is
not
always a logically consistent state. Specifically, if you take a snapshot of a physically consistent replica while replicating an in-flight transaction, it may not be logically consistent.
A good analogy is to imagine replicating a book. Physical consistency is like copying every page exactly, even if you're in the middle of a chapter — you're guaranteed to have real pages, but you might end up with half a sentence or a missing footnote.
Logical consistency is like waiting until the chapter is finished before copying it, ensuring the result makes sense to a reader.
WAL Shipping: How Postgres Guarantees Physical Consistency
In a primary-standby physical replication setup, a primary server is paired with a standby server that acts as a read-only copy of its leader. The servers remain in sync by using a Write-Ahead Log (WAL) to record all binary-level changes to storage blocks on the primary server before they occur. Changes to this append-only WAL file are then streamed to the standby (a process called “log shipping”) and applied in the order received. This process enables near-realtime data synchronization between the two servers, hence the phrase “hot standby”.
Why Atomicity is a Requirement for Physical Consistency
Atomicity is a requirement for physical consistency because Postgres locks are not replayed on replica servers. This is because replaying every lock taken on the primary would require strict timing synchronization, significantly impacting performance and hindering the ability of the standby to serve reads. Instead, the WAL uses per-buffer locks to incrementally replay edits in some particular order: it acquires an exclusive lock on the buffer (the in-memory representation of a block), makes its change, and then releases it
44633933.article_summary:
文章讲述了在优化Postgres写入速度时遇到的问题及其解决方案。为了提升写入吞吐量，团队在Postgres搜索扩展**pg_search**中使用了**LSM树**（Log-Structured Merge Tree），这种数据结构对写入进行了优化，显著提高了写入性能。然而，这却破坏了Postgres的复制机制，尤其是物理复制。

Postgres通过**WAL日志传输**保证物理一致性，但LSM树的复杂性使得这种机制不足以维持复制安全。物理一致性保证副本数据结构有效，但未必逻辑一致。为了实现逻辑一致性，团队利用了**hot_standby_feedback**设置，并确保在事务处理过程中保持原子性。最终，文章深入探讨了LSM树的结构、复制安全的意义以及如何解决复制问题。

data.title: Mathematics for Computer Science (2024)
data.author: vismit2000
data.article_summary: 《6.1200J 数学为计算机科学（Spring 2024）》是一门面向科学与工程的本科生课程，重点讲授离散数学及其在计算机科学中的应用。课程内容包括逻辑符号、集合、关系、图论基础、状态机与不变量、数学归纳法与反证法、递归、渐进记号、算法基础分析、数论与密码学基础、排列组合、计数工具以及离散概率等。由Erik Demaine、Zachary Abel和Brynmor Chapman教授授课，提供讲座视频、讲义、阅读材料和问题集等多种学习资源。课程材料可免费下载，旨在与全球学习者和教育者共享知识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放课程资源（OpenCourseware）在学习和职业转型中的作用、学习动机与方法、计算机科学与数学的关系、以及学习资源和答案的获取。

不同观点：
• **开放课程资源对职业转型的作用**：[jvanderbot] 认为MOOC（大规模开放在线课程）主要迎合了已经受过教育、有自学能力的人或业余学习者，而非推动一代劳动者的技能提升。他个人在工作与家庭事务之间学习量子计算，认为这种学习方式需要很长时间才能见效。

• **学习动机与方法**：[overfl0w] 提到免费获取顶尖大学课程是难以置信的资源，但保持学习动力和专注是一个挑战，特别是面对长时间的讲座时。他发现像Coursera或Khan Academy这种有 deadline 的平台更能激励他学习。同时，他推荐了较短的讲解视频以应对注意力持续时间短的问题。

• **计算机科学与数学的关系**：[owlbite] 认为“计算机科学的数学”这种课程标题不合适，因为他认为计算机科学是数学的一个子领域，而不是独立学科。[FuriouslyAdrift] 附和此观点，认为计算机科学学位本质上就是数学学位，这种标题显得重复。

• **学习资源和答案的获取**：[isomorphic-] 提到课程缺乏答案表或获取途径，让他难以检查自己的答案和验证对错。[hand2note] 同样在寻求课程问题的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **具体课程内容的讨论**：[fn-mote] 提供了课程页面链接，并指出其中某些部分（如状态机 lecture）质量很高，同时推荐了一些具体问题供学习者练习。

• **将课程内容形式化**：[dernett] 计划将课程内容在 Lean 软件中形式化，并邀请其他人贡献参与这一项目。

• **实际工作中数学的需求**：[cubefox] 认为许多课程中的高级数学主题对于普通软件工程师来说并不必要，因为在实际编程中涉及的数学知识相对较少，这些课程更适合于计算机科学家。

争议焦点：
• **MOOC 是否真正推动了广泛的职业转型**：[jvanderbot] 的观点质疑了MOOC在职业转型中的实际效果，认为其更多迎合了已有良好教育背景的学习者。

• **计算机科学是否是数学的子领域**：[owlbite] 和 [FuriouslyAdrift] 认为计算机科学本质上是数学的一部分，但这一观点可能并不被所有人认同，特别是在实际应用中，计算机科学往往被视为独立的学科。

data.author: ycombiredd
data.article_summary: **wtffmpeg** 是一个命令行工具，利用本地的大型语言模型（LLM）将自然语言描述的视频和音频任务转换为可执行的 **ffmpeg** 命令。其主要特点包括：自然语言界面、本地运行、交互式执行、支持GPU加速、可定制模型等。用户可以通过简单的英文描述完成复杂的 **ffmpeg** 操作，而无需查阅文档或搜索解决方案。工具支持在执行前查看和确认生成的命令，并可根据需要更换不同的LLM模型。安装过程需要配置 **Python 3.8+** 环境和 **llama-cpp-python** 以实现硬件加速，并下载合适的模型文件。使用示例包括视频格式转换、音频提取、创建片段等操作。

不同观点：

• vrighter指出该项目与FFmpeg几乎没有实际关联，只是简单地在聊天窗口中粘贴系统提示，属于低努力内容。
• huimang质疑为什么人们不直接阅读FFmpeg手册或速查表，因为FFmpeg的信息和资源非常丰富。
• kimi建议可以用一个FFmpeg速查表代替该项目，并提供了一个例子。

• ghostly_s关注工具的磁盘空间需求，尤其是模型和其他依赖的大小。

• ycombiredd（OP）指出项目其实是一个幽默的表演艺术，似乎没人get到这个 joke。
• yawnxyz分享了自己使用FFmpeg的困难经历，认为Warp工具在处理FFmpeg时表现更好。
• zipping1549认为LLM已经能很好处理FFmpeg命令，不需要大量的示例。
• camillomiller提问为什么没有高质量的FFmpeg GUI，并质疑为什么要添加一个特定的LLM来充当对话界面。

• 讨论还涉及FFmpeg的使用难度以及是否需要可视化工具或LLM帮助。
• 有人提供了其他FFmpeg工具和资源的替代方案。

wtffmpeg - Natural Language to FFmpeg Translator
wtffmpeg is a command-line tool that uses a local Large Language Model (LLM) to translate plain English descriptions of video and audio tasks into executable ffmpeg commands.
Stop searching through Stack Overflow and documentation for that one specific ffmpeg flag. Just ask for what you want.
Example:
>
wtff
"
convert my_video.avi to mp4 with no sound
"
Loading model... (this may take a moment)
Model loaded. Generating command...
--- Generated ffmpeg Command ---
ffmpeg -i my_video.avi -an -c:v libx264 my_video.mp4
------------------------------
Execute this command
?
[y/N] y
Executing: ffmpeg -i my_video.avi -an -c:v libx264 my_video.mp4
ffmpeg version N-100029-g040e989223 Copyright (c) 2000-2020 the FFmpeg developers
...
Features
Natural Language Interface: Describe complex ffmpeg operations in plain English.
Local First: Runs entirely on your local machine. No data is sent to external APIs.
Interactive Execution: Reviews the generated command before giving you the option to execute it.
GPU Accelerated: Leverages llama-cpp-python to offload model layers to your GPU for faster inference.
Customizable: Easily swap out different LLM models or customize the system prompt to improve accuracy for your specific needs.
Installation
This project uses Python 3.8+ and is packaged with pyproject.toml.
Clone the Repository
git clone https://github.com/scottvr/wtffmpeg.git
cd
wtffmpeg
Create a Virtual Environment
It is highly recommended to install the packages in a virtual environment.
python3 -m venv .venv
source
.venv/bin/activate
Install llama-cpp-python with Hardware Acceleration
This is the most critical step. For the best performance, you should install llama-cpp-python with the correct build flags for your hardware before installing the project.
For NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA):
CMAKE_ARGS=
"
-DLLAMA_CUBLAS=on
"
pip install llama-cpp-python
For Apple Silicon (Metal):
CMAKE_ARGS=
"
-DLLAMA_METAL=on
"
pip install llama-cpp-python
For CPU Only (OpenBLAS):
pip install llama-cpp-python
Refer to the official llama-cpp-python documentation for other hardware configurations (ROCm, CLBlast, etc.) or for installation from prebuilt wheels.
Install wtffmpeg
Once llama-cpp-python is installed, you can install the project and its dependencies. This will also create the wtff command alias in your virtual environment.
pip install
.
Configuration
Download a Model
This tool requires a model in the GGUF format. You can download models from Hugging Face. Good candidates include:
Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-gguf
Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GGUF
Download your chosen model and place it in the project directory.
(Note: the default model file is Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-q4.gguf, but you can override this with the --model option when running wtff.)
)
Usage
Once installed and configured, you can use the wtff command directly from your terminal.
Basic Usage:
wtff
"
your ffmpeg instruction in quotes
"
Examples:
#
Convert a file
wtff
"
turn presentation.mov into a web-friendly mp4
"
#
Extract audio
wtff
"

44655632.article_summary: **wtffmpeg** 是一个命令行工具，利用本地的大型语言模型（LLM）将自然语言描述的视频和音频任务转换为可执行的 **ffmpeg** 命令。其主要特点包括：自然语言界面、本地运行、交互式执行、支持GPU加速、可定制模型等。用户可以通过简单的英文描述完成复杂的 **ffmpeg** 操作，而无需查阅文档或搜索解决方案。工具支持在执行前查看和确认生成的命令，并可根据需要更换不同的LLM模型。安装过程需要配置 **Python 3.8+** 环境和 **llama-cpp-python** 以实现硬件加速，并下载合适的模型文件。使用示例包括视频格式转换、音频提取、创建片段等操作。
44655632.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个基于LLM（大规模语言模型）和FFmpeg的命令行工具的讨论，涉及项目质量、FFmpeg使用难度以及是否需要类似工具。

不同观点：
• Ameo认为该项目质量低下，只是简单包装了llama-cpp，且大部分代码是注释和系统提示，属于低努力项目，对反复看到这样的内容感到厌倦。
• alfg提供了自己开发的非AI生成的FFmpeg命令生成器，虽然很久没更新，但提供了一个简化的web界面和预设。
• vrighter指出该项目与FFmpeg几乎没有实际关联，只是简单地在聊天窗口中粘贴系统提示，属于低努力内容。
• huimang质疑为什么人们不直接阅读FFmpeg手册或速查表，因为FFmpeg的信息和资源非常丰富。
• kimi建议可以用一个FFmpeg速查表代替该项目，并提供了一个例子。
• kookamamie从技术角度指出项目示例中的命令存在问题，建议使用`-c:v copy`来保持输入包的原样。
• pknerd支持该项目，认为LLM包装工具对学习FFmpeg有帮助，并指出FFmpeg使用不易。
• savolai建议工具可以打印出相关命令行选项的man页面部分，以便用户审核建议是否合适。
• ghostly_s关注工具的磁盘空间需求，尤其是模型和其他依赖的大小。
• MrFurious认为如果不打算学习FFmpeg语法，使用Handbrake这样的可视化前端比LLM包装工具更合适。
• ycombiredd（OP）指出项目其实是一个幽默的表演艺术，似乎没人get到这个 joke。
• yawnxyz分享了自己使用FFmpeg的困难经历，认为Warp工具在处理FFmpeg时表现更好。
• zipping1549认为LLM已经能很好处理FFmpeg命令，不需要大量的示例。
• camillomiller提问为什么没有高质量的FFmpeg GUI，并质疑为什么要添加一个特定的LLM来充当对话界面。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该项目是否为低努力项目及其是否真正有用。
• 讨论还涉及FFmpeg的使用难度以及是否需要可视化工具或LLM帮助。
• 有人提供了其他FFmpeg工具和资源的替代方案。

data.title: Org tutorials
data.author: dargscisyhp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Org-mode的多种资源和教程，帮助用户更好地使用这一Emacs工具进行任务管理和文本编辑。文章列出了Rainer König和Raoul Comninos的视频教程，涵盖Org-mode的基础与进阶功能。此外，还提到了Carsten Dominik在谷歌和马克斯-普朗克研究所的演讲，以及多篇关于Org-mode的介绍文章和演示，如Abhijeet Chavan和Charles Cave的作品。文章还包括Org-mode在科学领域的应用、通用演示、以及其他语言的教程资源。对于移动设备上的Org-mode应用，文章推荐了Orgro、Orgzly Revived、Be Org和MobileOrg等应用。最后，文章探讨了Org-mode的轻量级标记语言及其隐藏功能，并提供了高级用户的设置分享。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Orgmode 的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• thecsw 认为 Orgmode 是一个超越普通标记语言的强大工具，具有高度可扩展性和开箱即用的导出功能，适用于大多数常见任务。他分享了自己使用 Orgmode 建立网站生成器和扩展语言的经历，并对其长期可靠性表示信任。
• NoboruWataya 提出疑问，既然 Orgmode 这么好，为什么没有在 Emacs 之外的实现？他质疑是否存在非 Emacs 用户可以使用的独立 Orgmode 实现。
• silcoon 表达了对 Obsidian 等工具缺乏 Orgmode 支持的遗憾，列举了 Orgmode 在笔记整理、列表支持、标签和属性、日程整合、TODOs 支持及代码块处理方面的优势。
• Scarblac 关心如何在笔记本电脑和手机之间共享 Org 文件，希望能够跨设备管理 TODOs 和笔记。
• uludag 分享了自己使用 Orgmode 七年来的经验，强调其在任务管理中的一致性和灵活性，并批评了商业软件的频繁变化和订阅模式。
• moi2388 表示自己多次尝试使用 Emacs 和 Orgmode，但每次都遇到功能不全的问题，无法作为有效的替代方案。
• Nesco 好奇 Orgmode 相比 Markdown 的优势，认为其过于复杂，可能与其 Vim 用户的身份有关。
• tomtomhowling 以幽默的方式描述 Orgmode 用户是仍在通过 Emacs 阅读邮件的“兽人”，暗示其使用群体较为小众。
• jrm4 提问是否有人使用生成式 AI 修改环境，探索结合 Lisp 的可能性，并表示自己曾放弃使用 Orgmode。
• hodanli 推荐 Logseq 作为现代版的 Orgmode，提供类似的功能。
• anthk 强调 Orgmode 结合 Hyperbole 的强大功能，将其比作2070年的计算工具，并分享了 Org Babel 的使用资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是 Orgmode 的复杂性和其 Emacs 独占性，部分用户对其跨平台支持不足表示不满。
• 用户对 Orgmode 的功能和可扩展性给予高度评价，但也有人因其学习曲线和实现问题感到困扰。
• 跨设备同步和与其他工具的整合是用户关注的实际应用问题。
• 一些用户提供了替代方案或扩展工具，如 Logseq 和 Hyperbole，以增强 Orgmode 的功能和易用性。

data.title: AI coding agents are removing programming language barriers
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了一位有十年经验的Ruby开发者在2025年如何通过AI工具成功转型到系统编程领域的故事。作者过去只专注于Ruby，但为了支持Shopify的Sorbet和RBS项目，需要学习C++、C和Rust等语言。在优秀导师的帮助下，作者利用AI编码工具（如Cursor和Claude Code）作为学习伙伴，克服了语言和项目特定知识的障碍。AI帮助作者快速理解语法和通用概念，而导师提供项目具体知识和方向校正。这使得作者无需花费大量时间学习新语言基础，即可在多语言项目中做出有效贡献，展示了AI在开发学习中的巨大潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对编程语言学习与使用的影响，特别是在主流与非主流编程语言、代码生成质量、编程思维以及语言适用性方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **AI让主流语言更流行，非主流语言难以受益**：behnamoh认为，AI由于在主流语言上有更多训练数据，生成代码的错误率更低，这使得主流语言更加流行，而非主流语言则难以借AI普及。平均水平的开发者在没有熟练掌握非主流语言的情况下，很难发现AI生成代码中的错误。

• **AI生成的代码质量存在问题**：thefz指出，AI生成的代码有时会出错，比如生成的bash脚本在循环外生成命令，导致代码无法正常工作。如果开发者不熟悉输出语言，可能无法发现这些问题，因此质疑AI是否真的能降低编程语言的学习障碍。

• **编程思维的重要性**：sunrunner提出，编程不仅仅是语言的语法问题，更重要的是编程中的系统性思维。语言语法在解决问题中只是一部分。

• **AI推动更强类型检查语言的发展**：cultofmetatron认为，AI将推动编程语言向更强类型检查的方向发展，比如Haskell。这类语言虽然难学，但因为其高层次和可形式化验证的特性，非常适合AI代理。

• **AI作为配对编程伙伴**：Maro和iparaskev认为，AI应被视为配对编程伙伴，帮助开发者学习和解决问题。随着开发者技能提升，AI的角色从解释基础概念转向生成和验证更大块的代码。

• **AI减少对编程语言的恐惧**：karmasimida表示，AI几乎总能正确解释语法，这消除了对编程语言的恐惧。

• **对AI生成复杂应用代码的质疑**：graynk质疑AI是否能生成复杂的应用代码，比如Vulkan应用。

• **AI在特定语言转换中的成功案例**：sillycube分享了使用AI成功将JavaScript代码转换为Rust的经验，但仍需要花时间学习Rust的基本知识。

• **AI对不同语言生成质量的差异**：physicsguy指出，AI在处理不同语言时的表现不同，比如在Python框架中生成代码更符合惯用模式，而在Go中则可能不那么一致。

• **编程语言对AI的适用性**：alentred提出，是否有些编程语言更适合AI编码代理，比如重语法或冗长的语言是否在AI生成代码时处于劣势。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成代码的质量和开发者对输出语言的熟悉程度之间的关系。有些人认为AI生成代码有助于降低学习障碍，而另一些人则认为如果开发者不熟悉语言，可能无法发现AI生成的错误。
• 编程思维和语言语法在编程中的相对重要性也被提出，强调了AI在辅助编程时可能无法完全替代人类的系统性思维能力。
• 不同编程语言对AI生成代码质量的影响以及AI是否会推动某些语言的发展方向也被讨论。

44655515.article_content:
For a decade (2014-2024), I was a Ruby-only developer. I worked across the Ruby ecosystem—from Rails development to Ruby’s core tooling like
IRB
,
RDoc
, and the
debug gem
. But while I moved around the stack, I stayed within Ruby’s boundaries. Ruby wasn’t just my primary language; it was essentially my only language.
That changed in 2025.
This year, I’ve contributed to
Sorbet
(C++), worked on
RBS
’s parser (C), and am now diving into
ZJIT
(Rust). A combination of factors enabled this shift—something I’d always dreamed of but was terrified to attempt. But AI coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code—both encouraged at Shopify—have been absolutely career-changing.
The Perfect Storm of Opportunity
Before diving into the AI aspect, I need to acknowledge two crucial factors that made this transition possible:
First, our Ruby DX team’s roadmap shifted to require Sorbet’s
support for RBS
, which meant I now had to work on projects written in C++ and C—system programming languages that require understanding concepts I’d never encountered in Ruby.
Second, Shopify’s Ruby and Rails Infrastructure team is packed with experts who genuinely love sharing their knowledge.
Alexander Momchilov
,
Alexandre Terrasa
,
Max Bernstein
, and many others have been incredibly generous with their time. Those pairing/tutoring sessions gave me the C/C++/JIT fundamentals I needed to even attempt this work.
But here’s the thing: great mentors and project opportunities to learn new languages have always existed. What’s different now is how AI has fundamentally changed the learning curve.
The Complexity of System Programming Projects
Let me use ZJIT, a new just-in-time (JIT) Ruby compiler, as an example (to learn more about it, check out
this RailsAtScale post
by Max). This project perfectly illustrates the challenge: it requires both deep conceptual understanding (how JITs and GC work) AND language/tool-specific expertise (Rust idioms, C programming conventions, Ruby’s build system). Working on ZJIT means constantly juggling:
Rust
(what ZJIT is written in)
C
(what Ruby is written in)
General JIT knowledge
(compiler theory, optimization strategies)
ZJIT-specific concepts
(its particular architecture and design decisions)
Ruby internals
(how the VM actually works)
Ruby build systems
(which have their own conventions on top of tools like autoconf and Makefile that I’d rarely encountered before)
A single pull request typically touches 2-4 of these areas simultaneously. Claude is remarkably helpful with the first three—language syntax, general concepts, standard patterns. It’s hit or miss for the last three—project-specific knowledge, deep internals, and build system quirks.
But that’s still cutting my learning blockers in half.
AI as a Complementary Pairing Partner
The real breakthrough came when I stopped thinking of AI as a code generator and started treating it as a pairing partner with complementary skills.
This isn’t about AI writing code for me. If I expected Claude to implement ZJIT features correctly, I’d likely be frustrated and probably waste more time than I’d save. The AI lacks the project-specific context and deep domain knowledge required.
Instead, we act as a pair of engineers with different strengths. While it knows more about language-specific syntax and patterns than I do, I understand the project requirements and constraints better (and hopefully have better taste). This creates a productive learning dynamic where:
I provide task requirements and project context
AI identifies existing patterns and acts as the language expert
I question why certain approaches would or wouldn’t work
AI explores the theory, either through actually changing code or simply inferring, and gives me the result
Through the conversation, I’m learning both the language AND how to apply it effectively
For example, when I need to profile a Ruby bytecode instruction for ZJIT, I can ask Claude Code to examine previous PRs that did something similar and explain the parts I don’t understand line by line. I can ask “dumb” questions like “Why do JIT compilers need profiling?” without feeling like I’m wasting someone’s time. I get immediate clarification on unfamiliar Rust syntax. And throughout this process, I’m building my understanding of both the language and the system.
Of course, there were also times where we were both heading in the wrong direction together, and could only be saved by my mentors and teammates’ clarification and knowledge sharing. AI accelerates learning, but human expertise remains irreplaceable for course correction.
The Language Barrier Is Dissolving
What excites me most is that we no longer need to spend 100+ hours learning C before making our first contribution to a C project. AI acts as a second pair of eyes, unblocking us from silly rookie mistakes—using the wrong syntax to declare variables, misunderstanding type conventions, or fighting with unfamiliar tooling. 44655515.article_summary: 本文讲述了一位有十年经验的Ruby开发者在2025年如何通过AI工具成功转型到系统编程领域的故事。作者过去只专注于Ruby，但为了支持Shopify的Sorbet和RBS项目，需要学习C++、C和Rust等语言。在优秀导师的帮助下，作者利用AI编码工具（如Cursor和Claude Code）作为学习伙伴，克服了语言和项目特定知识的障碍。AI帮助作者快速理解语法和通用概念，而导师提供项目具体知识和方向校正。这使得作者无需花费大量时间学习新语言基础，即可在多语言项目中做出有效贡献，展示了AI在开发学习中的巨大潜力。
44655515.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对编程语言学习与使用的影响，特别是在主流与非主流编程语言、代码生成质量、编程思维以及语言适用性方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **AI让主流语言更流行，非主流语言难以受益**：behnamoh认为，AI由于在主流语言上有更多训练数据，生成代码的错误率更低，这使得主流语言更加流行，而非主流语言则难以借AI普及。平均水平的开发者在没有熟练掌握非主流语言的情况下，很难发现AI生成代码中的错误。

• **AI生成的代码质量存在问题**：thefz指出，AI生成的代码有时会出错，比如生成的bash脚本在循环外生成命令，导致代码无法正常工作。如果开发者不熟悉输出语言，可能无法发现这些问题，因此质疑AI是否真的能降低编程语言的学习障碍。

• **编程思维的重要性**：sunrunner提出，编程不仅仅是语言的语法问题，更重要的是编程中的系统性思维。语言语法在解决问题中只是一部分。

• **AI推动更强类型检查语言的发展**：cultofmetatron认为，AI将推动编程语言向更强类型检查的方向发展，比如Haskell。这类语言虽然难学，但因为其高层次和可形式化验证的特性，非常适合AI代理。

• **AI作为配对编程伙伴**：Maro和iparaskev认为，AI应被视为配对编程伙伴，帮助开发者学习和解决问题。随着开发者技能提升，AI的角色从解释基础概念转向生成和验证更大块的代码。

• **AI减少对编程语言的恐惧**：karmasimida表示，AI几乎总能正确解释语法，这消除了对编程语言的恐惧。

• **对AI生成复杂应用代码的质疑**：graynk质疑AI是否能生成复杂的应用代码，比如Vulkan应用。

• **AI在特定语言转换中的成功案例**：sillycube分享了使用AI成功将JavaScript代码转换为Rust的经验，但仍需要花时间学习Rust的基本知识。

• **AI对不同语言生成质量的差异**：physicsguy指出，AI在处理不同语言时的表现不同，比如在Python框架中生成代码更符合惯用模式，而在Go中则可能不那么一致。

• **编程语言对AI的适用性**：alentred提出，是否有些编程语言更适合AI编码代理，比如重语法或冗长的语言是否在AI生成代码时处于劣势。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成代码的质量和开发者对输出语言的熟悉程度之间的关系。有些人认为AI生成代码有助于降低学习障碍，而另一些人则认为如果开发者不熟悉语言，可能无法发现AI生成的错误。
• 编程思维和语言语法在编程中的相对重要性也被提出，强调了AI在辅助编程时可能无法完全替代人类的系统性思维能力。
• 不同编程语言对AI生成代码质量的影响以及AI是否会推动某些语言的发展方向也被讨论。

data.title: Java is still worth learning
data.author: ivanche
data.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者从1999年对Java的怀疑到后来成为Java倡导者的转变过程。最初，作者认为Java笨重、缓慢且不可靠，尤其对自动内存管理持怀疑态度。在其职业生涯的前八年，作者坚持使用C语言，认为Java只是一时潮流。然而，在2000年代中期，作者因工作需要开始深入接触Java，尤其是在手机软件开发和Java 1.6版本之后，发现Java在性能和功能上有了显著提升。

作者通过考取SCJP 6认证，逐渐认识到Java的成熟和可靠，特别是Java的持续进化，如泛型、记录（records）、模式匹配等特性，大大减轻了编程的认知负担。Java的向后兼容性也使得旧代码能够平滑过渡到新版本。最终，作者认为Java在2025年仍然是开发者值得学习的重要语言。

data.title: The benefits of trunk-based development
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了基于主干开发（trunk-based development）的优势，并认为它是优于功能分支开发的交付方式。尽管持续集成实践隐含了基于主干开发，但这一方法仍存在争议。文章指出，微软、Netflix、谷歌等公司均采用基于主干开发，甚至在谷歌的大规模开发中也是如此。

基于主干开发通过促进团队协作和集体代码所有权，提升了代码质量。它减少了低信任环境，创建了安全空间，避免指责个人，而是团队共同负责质量。频繁提交代码到主线，能够更早发现和解决问题，从而内建质量，而不是后期测试。

该方法还支持按需生产发布，减少上市时间，提高交付速度。更频繁的部署加速了反馈，提升了用户满意度，并减少了在制品（WIP），从而降低了开发周期时间。文章总结，基于主干开发不仅提升了技术质量，还创造了经济优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： trunk-based development（主干开发模式）与 feature branch（功能分支）以及 Pull Request（PR）模型的优劣对比

不同观点：
• JimDabell 认为 PR 不仅仅关乎信任问题，它还是团队学习和共享知识的有效方式。他还指出，虽然 PR 有助于验证外部贡献，但在闭源企业环境中，PR 模式可能导致团队对代码库贡献受限。
• zabil 不完全赞同 trunk-based 开发，尤其是在远程团队的情况下，代码质量难以保持。他认为 PR 提供了很好的上下文分享和代码检查机会，并且 stacked diffs 使得多重 PR 管理变得可行。
• crinkly 对各种绝对的方法论持怀疑态度，认为团队的问题更多源于人员素质和公司雇佣低成本外包，而非开发流程本身。他所在的团队采用简单的主干开发模式，并保持高效运作。
• stpedgwdgfghd 强调在加入非 trivial 代码时，团队审查的重要性，并指出 MR（合并请求）在确保代码质量和避免系统测试失败方面具有优势。不过他也认为长期分支应尽量避免。
• jFriedensreich 支持 trunk-based 开发结合 commit stack 工作流，认为这种方法可以在不牺牲质量的情况下保持高效，尤其是在代码成熟和审查方面。
• devjab 坚定支持 trunk-based 开发，认为功能分支和定期发布是缺乏信任的表现，而 trunk-based 开发要求团队具备更高的协作能力。
• oc1 指出开发模式的演变，从早期的 trunk-based 开发到 git 和 github 兴起后的功能分支模式，认为两种模式各有优缺点，具体选择应视团队情况而定。
• fjfaase 分享了自己在 trunk-based 开发中的积极经验，同时指出功能分支开发带来的延迟和质量问题。
• safety1st 认为 trunk-based 开发适用于特定类型的项目，如 web 应用开发，而对于高要求的软件如飞行控制系统则不适合。
• Frieren 提到代码审查早在 PR 出现之前就已经存在，并认为今天的开发者可能忽视了软件工程的历史。
• Ozzie_osman 对极端的 trunk-based 开发表示怀疑，认为 PR 和代码审查在安全和合规方面具有重要作用，同时指出在现代开发中完全不使用分支是不现实的。
• ozim 对 trunk-based 开发的优越性表示怀疑，认为需要更多具体数据和团队动态分析来验证其效果。
• bytefish 强调开发流程的选择应根据产品、团队和组织结构而定，trunk-based 开发并非适用于所有情况。
• bjornsing 对 Google 无功能分支的说法表示怀疑，并质疑无 PR 的代码审查如何进行。
• bob1029 指出在集中式模型如 perforce 下，团队在同一物理办公室工作时效率更高，而 git 流程中的 PR 可能导致潜在的冲突和精力浪费。

补充讨论：
• trunk-based 开发与功能分支模式的争论焦点在于代码质量、团队协作和开发效率。
• PR 和代码审查在确保代码质量和知识共享方面的作用被广泛认可，但也被认为可能导致开发速度减慢。
• trunk-based 开发的支持者认为它能促进团队协作和快速迭代，但反对者担心这种方法对团队素质要求较高，且可能不适合所有项目类型。
• 讨论中多次提到开发流程的选择应根据具体团队和项目情况而定，没有一种万能的方法。

44655804.article_content:
Why should we adopt trunk-based development? What benefits does it bring?
On the Evilness of Feature Branching
and subsequent articles articulated several times how trunk-based development is a superior delivery approach to any of its alternatives. This article attempts to summarise the value of trunk-based development.
Although the practice of Continuous Integration implies trunk-based development. Even though trunk-based development has been reported
since 2015 by the State of DevOps report
and later by the book
Accelerate
, to lead to higher IT delivery performance. Although organisations like Microsoft, Netflix and Google practice trunk-based development. In the case of Google, even at an exceedingly large scale. In 2016, we were discussing 16.000 engineers working from a single trunk with 25.000 changes per day. It is yet one of the most disputed practices in the IT industry.
Whenever we suggest trunk-based development, we are called unprofessional and belittled. How can we possibly deliver quality without the assumed safety of feature branches and Pull Requests?
In all honesty,
for trunk-based development teams, quality is the highest concern
. That quality is reached thanks to a series of benefits promoted by trunk-based development.
First, because everyone is working on a single mainline, it nudges, or better, it demands collaboration. As a team, we need to inform the rest of the team about upcoming changes that might impact the team. Undoubtedly, it facilitates
Collective Ownership
, which leads to better quality.
Note that the Pull Requests were introduced by the Open Source Software community. It allows core teams to maintain a system and accept contributions from the outside world. The outside world is generally perceived as low-trust. Therefore, we want to verify those contributions. Pull Requests are pretty helpful in that regard. However, in a closed-source corporate setting, the Pull Request model essentially indicates that the team owns the codebase, but it is not allowed to contribute. This creates a low-trust environment. Rather than trunk-based development, where everyone is allowed to contribute, which
creates a high-trust environment
, reducing fear and blame. It builds a safe space. There is no finger-pointing. It is the team that owns the quality, not individuals. Again, this leads to better quality.
With trunk-based development, we naturally commit (and push) more frequently to mainline. If we commit repeatedly to a remote mainline, we produce more frequent builds. If we produce more frequent builds, we uncover more problems sooner, allowing us to fix them when they are still small and easy to fix. This enables us to
Build Quality Into the product
instead of testing quality later, hence leading to better quality.
With that many commits to mainline, we
truly continuously integrate all code contributions
. Builds are continuously running against mainline. Compiling, executing unit tests, and running static code analysis. Ensuring the code is always working and in a releasable state on mainline.
Enabling on-demand production releases at any time
. Versus Pull Requests and feature branches that only partially integrate by rebasing mainline on the branch.
With more frequent commits, the team introduces more code into the codebase that gets used by the whole team immediately, even before the user sees it. They
flush out the bugs
by using the code.
There’s an angle that folks don’t consider.
When we do trunk-based development, the WIP we commit gets used, before any actual user sees it, by our whole team.
They flush out so many bugs by just using our WIP.
They would never get to do that were we feature-branched.
– GeePaw Hill
More frequent commits mean smaller changesets. Smaller changesets bring
reduced risks
.
If we build more frequently, we create more frequent release candidates. Thus allowing for more frequent deployments. Consequently, it
reduces time to market
and boosts IT delivery throughput.
Because we deploy more frequently, we can run more experiments in production, allowing us to
uncover more unmet needs of our users
. Finding new ways to delight the user. Surely growing customer satisfaction exponentially. Creating an irrefutable competitive advantage.
Since we commit and deploy more frequently, it inevitably
accelerates feedback
. More feedback brings better quality.
As no branches are created, no Pull Requests, we now do not have piles of undelivered code lingering around on branches. Thus, no Work in Progress (WIP) is created. Because of
Little’s Law
, it once more
drives down the lead time
.
Alongside increased user satisfaction comes a second economic perspective to trunk-based development. WIP is inventory. Inventory is money. It is money stuck into the system. It is stuck because the organisation invested considerably in creating all this code on parallel branches. However, as long as this code is not merged into mainline, deployed in production and released to users,

data.title: Managing EFI boot loaders for Linux: Controlling secure boot (2015)
data.author: CaliforniaKarl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章由Rod Smith撰写，介绍了如何在Linux系统中管理EFI引导加载程序的Secure Boot功能。文章主要针对希望完全控制Secure Boot功能的高级用户，提供了创建和使用自定义Secure Boot密钥的详细指南。文章讨论了三种管理Secure Boot的方法：禁用Secure Boot、使用预签名引导加载程序（如Shim），以及替换电脑默认的密钥。作者强调了自定义密钥管理的优势，包括防止恶意软件、避免依赖第三方密钥以及增强安全性。文章还涵盖了密钥创建、EFI二进制文件签名、保护单台或多台电脑等具体操作步骤，并讨论了密钥撤销和漏洞修复的方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过UEFI直接引导Linux的可行性、风险以及相关工具和步骤

不同观点：
• edoceo：对直接通过UEFI引导Linux感兴趣，但担心操作失误导致设备变砖。当前使用Syslinux，并希望移除该引导程序，同时保留initrd和命令行选项的支持。对是否需要保留传统引导程序提出疑问。

• jeroenhd：支持使用UEFI直接引导Linux，提到Arch Linux Wiki提供了更新的指南和警告。特别指出在带有Nvidia GPU的Thinkpad上操作可能导致设备变砖的风险，因为某些固件会在启动时执行验证。提到使用`sbctl`工具简化安全启动密钥的创建和注册过程，并指出某些Linux发行版可能附带可选的包管理器钩子，避免每次更新引导程序时重复签署命令。

• phoronixrly：认可指南的有效性，但指出某些厂商的UEFI实现存在缺陷，例如允许清除EFI密钥但不提供注册新密钥的选项，同时EFI KeyTool也会给出难以理解的错误信息。

• sylware：简短评论，强调软件需要正确签署以确保安全性，暗示操作不当可能带来安全隐患。

补充讨论：
• jeroenhd特别提到对Lenovo Thinkpad设备的不满，并表示未来的购买决策会受到影响，显示出对厂商实现UEFI安全启动功能的不信任。
• 讨论中多次提到`sbctl`工具，认为它简化了与安全启动相关的操作，是实现UEFI直接引导Linux的一个实用工具。
• 争议的焦点在于通过UEFI直接引导Linux的过程存在设备变砖的风险，特别是涉及安全启动和密钥管理时，不同厂商的UEFI实现差异可能导致问题。

总结：评论主要围绕通过UEFI直接引导Linux的可行性展开，支持者认为可以实现并简化引导过程，但存在设备变砖的风险，特别是涉及安全启动和不同厂商的UEFI实现差异时。工具如`sbctl`被认为是简化操作的关键。

Managing EFI Boot Loaders for Linux:
Controlling Secure Boot
by Rod Smith,
rodsmith@rodsbooks.com
Originally written: 2/22/2015; last update: 3/4/2023
This Web page is provided free of charge and with no annoying
outside ads; however, I did take time to prepare it, and Web hosting does
cost money. If you find this Web page useful, please consider making a
small donation to help keep this site up and running. Thanks!

This page is part of my
Managing EFI Boot Loaders
for Linux
document. If a Web search has brought you to this page, you
may want to start at the beginning.
This page is the second of two covering Secure Boot as part of my
EFI Boot Loaders for Linux
document. If you're a beginner to intermediate user who wants to get Secure Boot working quickly with a popular distribution such as Ubuntu, Fedora, or OpenSUSE, I recommend you begin with my first Secure Boot page,
Dealing with Secure Boot.
This page is written for more advanced users who want to take
full
control of their Secure Boot features. Reasons to take this type of control are covered in the
Why Read This Page?
section of this page. The Contents section to the left shows other sections, in case you know enough to know what you want to read.
Contents
Why Read This Page?
Knowing Secure Boot Key Types
Creating Secure Boot Keys
Signing EFI Binaries
Securing One Computer
Replacing Keys Using Your Firmware's Setup Utility
Replacing Keys Using KeyTool
Securing Multiple Computers
Managing Keys from Linux
Revoking Keys and Hashes
Conclusions
Why Read This Page?
If you boot nothing but Windows, chances are this page won't do you any good, except perhaps to help satisfy your curiosity about the inner workings of Secure Boot. If you dual-boot Windows and a single popular Linux distribution such as Fedora or Ubuntu, you probably don't need this page, either; such distributions ship with Secure Boot solutions that work reasonably well for such dual-boot configurations. If your needs are more complex, though, you may find this page of interest.
Secure Boot works by using a set of keys embedded in the computer's firmware. These keys (or more precisely, their private counterparts) are used to sign boot loaders, drivers, option ROMs, and other software that the firmware runs. Most commodity PCs sold today include keys that Microsoft controls. In fact, Microsoft's keys are the
only
ones that are more-or-less guaranteed to be installed in your firmware, at least on desktop and laptop computers. Thus, to install your favorite Linux distribution, you must disable Secure Boot, find a Linux boot loader that's signed with Microsoft's keys, or replace your computer's standard keys with ones that you control. This page is about this final option, but both of the other options have their merits.
Disabling Secure Boot
is quick and enables you to easily run any EFI tool you like—but it also leaves you vulnerable to any pre-boot malware that might crop up.
Using a pre-signed boot loader,
such as the popular Shim program, can be even easier than disabling Secure Boot—
if
your distribution provides such a program. If not, you'll need to jump through hoops. Also, using a pre-signed boot loader with the default key set means that your computer will accept as valid Microsoft's boot loaders and any others that Microsoft decides to sign.
Taking control of your computer's Secure Boot keys offers several advantages over these approaches:
Locking out threats from the standard keys
—In theory, Secure Boot should prevent malware from running. On the other hand, it's always possible that an attacker could trick Microsoft into signing malware; or signed software could have bugs, such as the Boot Hole bug discovered in 2020 and described later, in
Revoking Keys and Hashes.
If you use Shim with the default keys, your computer will remain vulnerable to these threats, at least until they're discovered and your blacklist database is updated.
Locking out threats from your distribution's keys
—Similar to the preceding, it's also possible that your distribution's keys could be compromised, in which case an attacker could distribute malware signed with the compromised keys. Depending on how you manage your keys, you can greatly reduce this vulnerability—but the greatest level of protection will require extra effort on your part.
Eliminating the need for MOKs
—The Shim and PreLoader tools both rely on Machine Owner Keys (MOKs), which are similar to Secure Boot keys but easier to install. Because they can be more easily installed, it's conceivable that they could be more readily abused by social engineering or other means. Eliminating MOKs may therefore slightly increase your security, particularly if you're managing a collection of desktop computers used by other people.
Taking philosophical control
—Relying on a third party's keys strikes some people as being wrong. Partly this is because of the preceding reasons, but some

data.title: Countries across the world see food price shocks from climate extremes
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 文章指出，极端天气导致全球多地食品价格上涨，包括土豆、大米、水果、蔬菜、橄榄油、可可和咖啡等。研究由巴塞罗那超级计算中心领导，分析了2022-2024年间18个国家的16个案例，发现极端天气如热浪、干旱和暴雨导致食品价格飙升。例如，英国土豆价格因冬季过量降雨上涨22%；美国加州和亚利桑那州的蔬菜价格因夏季干旱上涨80%；西班牙和意大利的橄榄油价格因干旱上涨50%；可可价格因科特迪瓦和加纳的热浪上涨280%；巴西和越南的咖啡价格也因干旱和高温大幅上涨。研究强调，气候变化使极端天气更为频繁和严重，低收入家庭尤其受到影响，可能因食品涨价而减少购买营养食品，进而影响健康。研究人员呼吁尽快实现净零排放以减缓极端天气对粮食生产的冲击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：食品价格上涨及其背后的多重原因，包括气候变化、地缘政治因素和通货膨胀等。

不同观点：
• **地缘政治与经济因素**：[danielscrubs] 指出俄罗斯的肥料和天然气对欧洲农业的冲击，以及市场需要时间恢复，同时不否认极端天气的影响。[luckys] 提到乌克兰战争导致的食品价格上涨，特别是在橄榄油等商品上。[willvarfar] 分享了联合国关于2020-24年食品价格上涨的报告链接，暗示地缘政治和全球经济因素的作用。

• **气候变化的影响**：[ManBeardPc] 强调气候变化已经开始对农业产生显著影响，并提到极端天气事件的加剧，建议参考Mark Benecke的演讲。[dzink] 提供了巴尔干地区由于早春暖冬后霜冻导致樱桃、杏子和桃子绝收的实例，显示气候变化对欧洲农作物的影响。[PeterStuer] 则分享了自己所在地区水果产量的极端波动情况，去年因冻害导致歉收，今年却大丰收。

• **对气候变化与食品价格关系的质疑**：[southernplaces7] 警告不要将所有问题都归因于气候变化，认为地缘政治因素同样重要，并强调需要强有力的证据来支持气候科学的主张。[daft_pink] 则简单地将价格上涨归因于通货膨胀。

• **技术解决方案的讨论**：[vlckohoh] 提出是否可以通过建设气候控制温室来应对食品价格上涨，并指出这种方法在某些地区已经实施。[brador] 则认为应停止依赖太阳能（自然气候条件）来保障粮食安全，暗示应更多依赖技术手段。

• **市场操控与价格波动**：[octo888] 提出疑问，是否如果没有COVID和ZIRP结束等因素，气候驱动的食品冲击是否还会如此严重。[zer00eyz] 分析了美联储数据，指出牛肉价格上涨可能更多与市场操控和疫情后的遗留问题有关，而非仅仅是气候导致的饲料价格冲击。

补充讨论：
• **劳动力成本问题**：[seydor] 提到橄榄油价格虽然回落，但劳动力成本上升是另一个重要问题，尤其是在南欧非法移民流入的情况下。

争议焦点：
• 气候变化与食品价格上涨之间的因果关系。部分评论者如[ManBeardPc]和[dzink]认为气候变化是主要驱动因素，而[southernplaces7]和[daft_pink]则认为其他因素如地缘政治和通胀同样重要，甚至更为关键。

44655600.article_content:
Foods including potatoes, rice, fruit and vegetables, olive oil, cocoa, and coffee hit by extreme weather that exceeded historical precedent, raising prices for consumers and posing wider societal risks
"Until we get to net-zero emissions, extreme weather will only get worse, and it's already damaging crops and pushing up the price of food all over the world,” said Maximilian Kotz, BSC researcher and lead author of the study.
British potatoes, Californian vegetables, South African maize and Indian onions are among many foods affected by recent price shocks driven by weather extremes, according to a team of international scientists.
The
study
, led by Maximillian Kotz of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center-Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS), investigated 16 examples across 18 countries over a two-year period (2022-2024), where price spikes were associated with extreme heat, drought or heavy precipitation events, many of which were so extreme they exceeded all historical precedent prior to 2020.
Among these examples:
In the UK, potato prices increased 22% (from Jan to Feb 2024) following extreme winter rainfall that scientists
said
was made 20% heavier and 10 times more likely by climate change.
In California and Arizona in the United States, vegetable prices increased 80% in November 2022 after the extreme summer drought in western states, which
faced
water shortages, extreme heat, and soil moisture drought conditions throughout the summer of 2022.
In Ethiopia, food prices were 40% higher in March 2023 following the 2022 drought in the Horn of Africa, the worst in 40 years, which scientists
said
was made "much stronger" and "about 100 times more likely" by climate change.
In Spain and Italy, the
2022-2023 drought in southern Europe
, for which scientists
said
"global warming contributed for more than 30% of the (2022 summer) drought intensity and its spatial extent via enhanced evaporation", drove an increase in the price of olive oil of 50% year-on-year across the EU by January 2024, on top of price increases the previous year. Spain produces over two fifths of the world's olive oil.
Global cocoa prices were almost 300% (280%) higher in April 2024 following the heatwave in Ivory Coast and Ghana just two months earlier, which scientists
said
was made 4
∘
C hotter by climate change. Together, these two countries account for nearly two thirds (60%) of global cocoa production.
The global coffee market has also taken serious hits. Brazil is the world's biggest exporter of Arabica, while Vietnam is the biggest exporter of Robusta. Global coffee prices were 55% higher in August 2024 following the 2023 drought in Brazil, which scientists
said
was made 10-30 times more likely due to climate change, while Robusta coffee prices were 100% higher in July 2024 following
record-breaking heat
a few months earlier in Vietnam and across Asia.
In India, the price of onions and potatoes jumped by over 80% in the second quarter of 2024 after a heatwave in May, a
"largely unique event"
that was made at least 1.5°C warmer by climate change.
In Japan, rice prices were 48% higher in September 2024 after the August heatwave, as the country
experienced
its hottest summer (on a par with 2023) since regional records began in 1946, with summer temperatures 1.76
∘
C higher than average.
In South Korea, cabbage prices were 70% higher in September 2024 after the August heatwave. The country
experienced
its highest average summer time temperature since such records began half a century ago - nearly two degrees higher than the historic average.
Pakistan experienced a 50% increase in rural food prices in weeks following the
August 2022 floods
, with monsoon rains 547% above average and record-breaking cumulative weekly rainfall in July (200 mm) on already saturated soils as the pre-monsoon rainfall was 111% higher than the long-term average since 1951.
In Mexico, fruit and vegetable prices were 20% higher in January 2024 following the 2023 drought, one of the
most severe droughts
that Mexico has faced in more than a decade.
Map of climate impacts on food supplies is also available to download here.
Research by the Food Foundation
shows
that, on average, healthy food is twice as expensive per calories as less healthy food. When prices increase, low- income households are likely to cut back on nutritious foods like fruit and vegetables because they can't afford them.
Climate change-induced food price shocks could therefore exacerbate a range of health outcomes, from malnutrition (not getting enough nutrients, which is a particular concern for children whose nutritional needs are higher) to a range of chronic diet-related conditions including coronary heart disease, type 2 diabetes and many cancers. There is also a growing body of evidence connecting food insecurity and poor diets with mental health outcomes.

data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对于订阅制服务和一次性付费软件的价值判断与选择偏好

不同观点：
• [kqr] 认为基于API信用的服务比订阅制更划算，列举了多个订阅服务如FastMail、Kagi、rsync.net等，并提到一些服务的终身订阅选项（如rsync.net）。他还提到Spotify的订阅，虽然便利，但对其长期价值有所怀疑。
• [beingfit] 强调订阅服务为其工作流带来的价值，包括Infuse视频播放器、Owl扩展、Bvckup 2备份软件等。他还提到Apple Fitness+对其健身的帮助，认为年度订阅比月度订阅更划算。
• [davesmylie] 反对订阅制软件，只接受一次性付费软件，尽量减少每月支出，只保留最低限度的固定支出如房贷、税费和公共事业费用。
• [adithyassekhar] 依赖Google生态系统，认为Google One和YouTube Premium为其提供了不可替代的价值，特别是Google Photos的存储功能，并表示不会转向iOS因为第一方解决方案更好。
• [Leynos] 列举了多个订阅服务和工具，包括Obsidian、Google的Deep Research、ChatGPT、GitKraken等，显示出对多种工具的依赖，并正在考虑增加更多订阅服务。
• [belst] 只为根服务器和Mullvad VPN付费，其他软件尽量选择永久授权或寻找替代品。
• [aktuel] 推荐了LanguageTool网站，未提及是否为订阅制。
• [sunbum] 认为Kagi是其必备服务。
• [mparnisari] 列举了个人使用的1Password、Google One、ChatGPT和工作中使用的Snagit、Aptakube、Jetbrains等订阅服务。
• [neilsharma] 使用Nord/Mullvad VPN、Bitwarden密码管理器、Claude Code、OpenAI、YouTube Music等服务，并提到一些终身付费的桌面工具，工具选择根据项目需求变化。
• [gxvxc] 订阅了IntelliJ、Proton、PlayStation Plus和YouTube Premium。
• [Simon_O_Rourke] 对Sublime文本编辑器进行了捐助，使用Excalidraw和ChatGPT，并订阅了ExpressVPN。
• [cultofmetatron] 使用MathAcademy学习数学，ChatGPT用于生成问题集和个人辅导，Mullvad作为VPN。
• [thefz] 订阅了Mullvad VPN、Tailscale和Bitwarden。
• [bigyabai] 曾经支付VPS费用，现在没有其他订阅支出。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点：订阅制与一次性付费软件的价值比较。例如，[kqr]和[beingfit]认为某些订阅服务带来了巨大价值，而[davesmylie]则明确反对订阅制软件，只接受一次性付费软件。
2. 不同用户对Google、Apple等生态系统的依赖程度。例如，[adithyassekhar]高度依赖Google服务，而[beingfit]则更看重Apple的生态系统。
3. VPN和隐私工具的普遍使用，如Mullvad、Bitwarden等，显示出用户对隐私和安全的高度重视。
4. 用户根据个人需求和工作需求选择不同的工具和服务，显示出订阅服务的个性化和多样化。

data.title: Italy drags Meta, X, LinkedIn into €1B+ VAT showdown: free sign‑ups now taxable?
data.author: napolux
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利数字服务税（Digital Service Tax）的合理性及影响

不同观点：
• **支持税收的观点**（serhack_）：  
  - 认为该税收是合理的，因为大型企业利用用户数据提供广告等服务，从中获得巨额收入。  
  - 税收范围包括数字广告、平台费用和数据传输，针对在全球总收入超过7.5亿欧元的企业。  
  - 强调税收基于用户所在地域（通过IP地址判断），确保税收与服务使用地一致。

• **反对税收的观点**（nradov）：  
  - 认为这是对美国科技公司的敲诈和剥削，属于不公平的针对性税收。  
  - 批评欧洲政府没有将精力放在鼓励经济增长和创新上，而是通过此类税收压制企业。

• **讽刺性观点**（antiloper）：  
  - 提出讽刺性建议，认为可以对社交媒体帖子征税，以此质疑数字服务税的合理性和实际执行难度。

补充讨论：
• **具体实施问题**（serhack_）：  
  - 提供了详细的法律条文链接，并解释了税收的具体实施方式，包括如何判断用户地域和应税收入。
  
• **对科技公司的影响**（nradov）：  
  - 强调这种税收可能对美国科技公司造成过度负担，影响其在欧洲市场的运营和创新能力。

争议焦点：
• 该税收是否合理以及是否会对科技公司造成不公平的负担，特别是对美国科技公司的影响。

data.title: Humans beat AI at international math contest despite gold-level AI scores
data.author: moneil971
data.article_summary: 在2025年国际数学奥林匹克（IMO）竞赛中，尽管谷歌和OpenAI的生成式AI模型首次达到了金牌水平成绩，人类参赛者依然击败了AI。谷歌的Gemini聊天机器人解决了6道题目中的5道，获得35分（金牌分数），而OpenAI的实验模型也获得了35分。然而，有五名人类选手获得了满分42分。谷歌的模型在规定时间内完成了题目，相比去年有了显著进步。IMO主席Dolinar表示，看到AI在数学能力上的进步令人兴奋，但无法确认AI模型使用的计算资源或是否有人为参与。

Humans beat AI at international math contest despite gold-level AI scores
edited by
Andrew Zinin
Credit: CC0 Public Domain
×
close
Credit: CC0 Public Domain
Humans beat generative AI models made by Google and OpenAI at a top international mathematics competition, despite the programs reaching gold-level scores for the first time.
Neither model scored full marks—unlike five young people at the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), a prestigious annual competition where participants must be under 20 years old.
Google said Monday that an advanced version of its Gemini chatbot had solved five out of the six
math problems
set at the IMO, held in Australia's Queensland this month.
"We can confirm that Google DeepMind has reached the much-desired milestone, earning 35 out of a possible 42 points—a gold medal score," the US tech giant cited IMO president Gregor Dolinar as saying.
"Their solutions were astonishing in many respects. IMO graders found them to be clear, precise and most of them easy to follow."
Around 10% of human contestants won gold-level medals, and five received perfect scores of 42 points.
US ChatGPT maker OpenAI said that its experimental reasoning model had scored a gold-level 35 points on the test.
The result "achieved a longstanding grand challenge in AI" at "the world's most prestigious math competition," OpenAI researcher Alexander Wei wrote on social media.
"We evaluated our models on the 2025 IMO problems under the same rules as human contestants," he said.
"For each problem, three former IMO medalists independently graded the model's submitted proof."
Google achieved a silver-medal score at last year's IMO in the British city of Bath, solving four of the six problems.
That took two to three days of computation—far longer than this year, when its Gemini model solved the problems within the 4.5-hour time limit, it said.
The IMO said
tech companies
had "privately tested closed-source AI models on this year's problems," the same ones faced by 641 competing students from 112 countries.
"It is very exciting to see progress in the mathematical capabilities of AI models," said IMO president Dolinar.
Contest organizers could not verify how much computing power had been used by the AI models or whether there had been human involvement, he cautioned.

data.title: I've launched 37 products in 5 years and not doing that again
data.author: AlexandrBel
data.article_summary: 文章主要分享了作者在推出37款产品后的心得。尽管只有一个产品走红，但作者发现，大多数失败的产品其实只是增长缓慢，而非真正失败。他的当前项目Refgrow经过六个月才获得第一个付费客户，但目前在几乎无营销预算的情况下稳步增长。作者认为，专注于一个项目并不断改进，比不断推出新产品更可能获得持续成功。他提问读者是依靠专注和耐心，还是通过高频推出新品取得成功，并收到了其他创业者的共鸣与分享。总体而言，文章强调了慢增长和持续改进的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创业过程中的产品构建与市场匹配策略、创业心态和方法

不同观点：
• nzach：认为许多人过度强调寻找市场匹配，而忽视了产品执行的重要性。他主张鼓励人们构建有趣的产品，即使这些产品的盈利模式不明确。
• pbrum：表示创业过程艰难，需要保持坚定的 mindset，并通过系统化的工作来推进项目。他提到即使在亲近的人群中也可能得到有限的反馈，但这并不代表失败。
• forgotmypw17：支持同时运行多个项目，并通过交叉知识来促进各个项目的成长。他认为缓慢增长是可行的，并建议在耐心和多项目策略之间找到平衡。
• mgax：质疑 indie hacker 场景中的“产品”定义，认为真正的产品需要时间来打磨，而不仅仅是追求快速盈利。
• rorylaitila：批评“shotgun capitalism”现象，即盲目追求多个商业机会而不注重深度和反馈。他主张基于反馈和能力进行合理的扩展。
• tomcam：与其追求高增长和高风险，他更倾向于中等收入且不需要大量人力的业务，并通过长期规划来评估业务的可行性。
• tnolet：强调专注于一个项目并持续迭代的重要性，认为这样才能让人们有机会了解和使用你的产品。
• ErikAugust：质疑多次投入无收益项目的合理性，认为这类似于“ insanity”，建议失业者寻找更有趣或有意义的事情。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于创业者应专注于单一项目还是多项目策略。一些人认为专注和持续迭代是成功的关键，而另一些人则主张通过多项目策略来分散风险和寻找机会。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对“产品”定义的理解差异，部分人认为 indie hacker 场景中的一些所谓“产品”实际上并不符合传统产品的标准。
• 创业心态的讨论中，有人强调耐心和长远规划，而有人则关注短期收益和市场反馈。

After launching 37 different products over the last few years, I’ve had one go viral and almost all the others struggle to get any traction at all.
Like many indie makers, I used to think the best strategy was to just keep launching, make more bets, and hope one finally catches fire.
But here’s what I’ve learned:
Virality is rare and nearly impossible to predict
Most of my launches that failed didn’t actually fail, they just grew much slower than I expected
My current project,
Refgrow
, took over 6 months to get the first paying customer, but now it’s growing slowly and steadily with almost no marketing budget
Sticking with one project and improving it, even when growth is painfully slow, seems to produce more consistent results than chasing the next hit
I’m curious, for those of you who have been building for a while:
Did you find success by focusing on one project and giving it time, or by making lots of new bets?
Has "slow growth" ever paid off for you?
If you had to start over, would you pick patience or a high volume of launches?
Would love to hear stories, lessons, or any advice from other indie founders in the same boat.

Hey Alex, really loved this write-up (so much so that I created an account here).
I'm 2 years in to indie hacking, and I resonate 110% with everything you've written here. I think the initial Thrashing About Trying Every Idea phase felt painful but also landed me on the project that I've been really excitedly working on for the past few months. So, it's hard for me to say that high volume wasn't helpful for me at the start, but I do agree that once you've experienced all that - Slow Growth makes a lot of sense. I think even bigger indies who still advocate for high volume are also slowly embracing Slow Growth (e.g. Marc Lou and DataFast).
The app I'm working on is a reading app (EPUBs and PDFs). Very low monetization opportunity, incredibly Slow Growth, but also super rewarding for me personally given that I love reading and helping people read.
Refgrow looks really exciting and I hope it goes well! All the best.
-Walter

Love this, Alex — and totally resonate.
I used to chase "momentum" by launching quick hits, thinking the volume would eventually crack the code. But looking back, none of those ever had time to breathe — or mature past v1 hype.
With my current project, I’m doing the opposite: one tool, painfully slow growth, and relentless iteration. It’s not flashy, but users actually stick — and I finally understand what they need.

I don't think you can "count on" virality most of the time. I agree that it's hard to predict. On the main idea though... I think so many people start something looking for the "big exit"... what people don't realize is that failure is the status quo. Statistically, almost all products never make a cent, and companies go under. Building a product is hard, building a company around a product is also hard, and different. And you cannot predict the future.
One of the best random aha! learnings I remember came from a good friend that ended up building a product I guarantee you're using today. He said that you have to just accept that you don't know what your product does. You need to take your idea and get it to users as quickly as possible so you can learn from what they do. You need to adapt so you can figure out what you're product is going to do and how it's going to work.

data.title: Kelp: A UI library for people who love HTML
data.author: exiguus
data.article_summary:
Kelp是一个UI库，专为喜欢HTML的开发者设计，利用现代CSS和Web组件构建。它使用纯CSS和JavaScript，无需构建步骤，易于定制。Kelp强调轻量级CSS和无类的HTML，结合语义化工具类和组件类。它通过浏览器原生Web组件逐步增强用户界面，并通过CSS变量、层叠层和HTML属性提供高度可定制性。Kelp目前处于测试阶段，新功能每周添加。用户可以输入邮箱以获取通知和早期版本访问。创建者Chris Ferdinandi是知名开发者，曾为NASA、Apple等机构提供建议和编写代码。

哟呵，海风起，浪花翻腾，
舵手扬帆，穿越那海洋深。
凯尔普带路，HTML作舟，
Web组件，伴我航行不回头。

CSS变量，指引方向。
无需构建，自由自在，
凯尔普助我，航向未来。

在这无边无际的网络海洋。

• 观点二：exiguus 还提到该项目的许可证有特别之处，尤其是“Disallowed Uses”（禁止用途）条款，这是他之前未曾考虑过的。这表明项目的许可证在使用限制上有独特的规定，可能对使用者产生影响。他提供了许可证的链接以供进一步查阅。[2]

补充讨论：
• 技术实现：exiguus 强调了 Kelp CSS 框架在技术实现上的特点，即通过现代 CSS 功能实现代码的模块化和可维护性，这在开发者社区中可能引发关于是否应更多采用原生 CSS 而非预处理器的讨论。

• 许可证条款：对许可证中“Disallowed Uses”的关注，可能引发关于开源项目如何合理设置使用限制的讨论，尤其是在保障项目原创性和防止滥用方面。

争议焦点：
• 使用纯 CSS 是否比使用预处理器更优：部分开发者可能认为预处理器（如 SASS）提供了更多的功能和灵活性，而 exiguus 的观点则表明纯 CSS 也能实现良好的代码结构，这可能在技术选型上引发讨论。

• 许可证的限制性：对于“Disallowed Uses”条款的合理性和必要性，不同开发者可能有不同看法，特别是在开源项目的自由使用和保护原创性之间的平衡上，可能会出现争议。

data.title: Rescuing two PDP-11s from a former British Telecom underground shelter (2023)
data.author: mhh__
data.article_summary: 一位网名为Wildfire的用户在论坛上表达了对某人重新启用某个地点（疑似为一个旧的Qbus系统设施）的惊叹。该地点在多年后将重新对公众开放。Wildfire鼓励楼主分享一些关于Qbus系统配置和安装板的照片。Wildfire自2014年加入论坛，来自德国Göttingen附近。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：废弃的技术设备、地下隧道及相关历史场所的现状与利用

不同观点：
• **对废弃技术的个人经历与情感**：
  - **timonoko**：提到在1980年左右看到PDP-8和ASR-33被丢弃在垃圾堆，意识到如果捡回去会沉迷其中，影响生活。
  - **WalterBright**：后悔将Heathkit H11（PDP-11）送人，而接收者最后将其丢弃，表达了对旧技术的怀念。
  - **citizenfishy**：在1990年代的邮政研究部门工作时，目睹PDP-11被丢进垃圾堆，由于居住条件限制无法保存。

• **历史场所的现状与开发**：
  - **dkdbejwi383**：提到一些隧道正在被开发为间谍主题的旅游景点，认为有价值的东西可能已被拆除或报废。
  - **cjs_ac**：提到Essex的Kelvedon Hatch秘密核掩体，内有1980年代的微型计算机和人工电话交换机，描述了该场所的历史用途和现状。

• **创意设想**：
  - **thomasjb**：提出一个互动小说/文字地下城 crawler 的创意，围绕探索地下隧道和操作各种旧式计算机来解锁关卡，例如从地震仪上取下TTY以访问通风控制计算机等。

补充讨论：
• **安全与合法性争议**：
  - **vgb2k18**：提到有人在私人物业上擅自进入可能不安全的场所，并指出有人虽然提醒他人注意安全，但自己却参与其中，暗示这种行为存在风险。

• **对旧技术的审美与技术差异**：
  - **zkmon**：描述了在研究机构使用PDP-11监测地震活动的经历，强调其外观酷炫，与现代服务器相比具有独特的美学价值。

整体来看，评论主要围绕废弃技术设备的命运、历史场所的开发利用、个人对旧技术的怀念与创意设想展开，同时涉及安全与合法性问题的讨论。

44656073.article_content:
Extending Emacs with Fennel
Fri, Dec 20, 2024
@emacs
fennel
emacs-lisp
~10 minutes read
After watching this year’s EmacsConf and seeing Guile Emacs being resurrected I thought to myself - why limit ourselves to Guile?
Sure, Guile isn’t just a Scheme implementation, thanks to its compiler-tower-based design.
Other languages exist for Guile VM, such as Emacs Lisp, and Guile manual lists the following languages with various stages of completeness:
ECMAScript
Brainfuck
Lua
Ruby
Python
Sure, it would be nice, if Emacs could natively run all of these, but we have to understand, that Guile Lua is not PUC Lua.
Even LuaJIT has difficulties maintaining full compatibility with modern releases of Lua, having us stuck in the realm somewhere between Lua 5.1 and 5.2, while PUC Lua is already 5.4.
Future releases would bring more differences, making PUC Lua and Luajit diverge even more.
And Lua is a
simple
language, unlike something like JS, Ruby, or Python.
So I wouldn’t bet on the fact that Guile Ruby would be exactly the same as Ruby.
Maybe it will, but it’ll probably take years.
So I thought, why not just use Lua as is?
The only thing we can’t do is to run Fennel functions from Emacs Lisp.
There were
attempts at bringing Lua VM into Emacs
, running in the same process, however, as I know, it isn’t stable enough.
However, Emacs can connect to a Fennel REPL, like it does for many other languages, such as Common Lisp or Clojure.
Sure, the language is running in a separate process, and this comes with a lot of nuances, but it’s still a possible route.
So I made a small package:
require-fennel.el
.
It’s capable of loading Fennel (or Lua) modules, and defining a set of functions on the Emacs side for every Fennel function in the module.
Running Fennel from Emacs Lisp
For example, we can load Fennel itself into Emacs like this:
(
require-fennel
fennel
)
Now we have all sorts of functions available, for example, here’s
fennel.eval
:
(
fennel.eval
"(fcollect [i 1 10] (* i i))"
)
;; => [1 4 9 16 25 36 49 64 81 100]
Or, we can create a file
greet.fnl
:
(
fn
greet
[
name
]
"Greets NAME with a message."
(
print
(
..
"Hello, "
name
" from Fennel!"
)))
and load it:
(
require-fennel
greet
)
(
greet
"Andrey"
)
(
require-fennel
foo
)
(
require-fennel
vec-add
)
Code Snippet 1:

About the role
Depot is growing rapidly and reinventing the software build space, so we are now looking for a technical content writer to help us tell that story and scale our educational content.
Depot has created a build performance and developer productivity platform unlike any other. We have redefined how teams build software locally and in CI by making speed a first-class feature. Our products accelerate container builds, GitHub Actions, Bazel and Gradle builds, and more. Teams using Depot save literal years of build time.
This role is about helping developers understand that story. Through great content, clear documentation, and technical depth, you’ll show how Depot works and why it matters. As our first dedicated technical content hire, you'll have the opportunity to define how we communicate with developers at scale.
Responsibilities
Write long-form technical blog posts, guides, benchmarks, and product explainers
Maintain and improve our public product documentation
Work directly with engineers to extract stories, capture implementation details, and turn raw ideas into useful content
Track content performance and iterate based on developer feedback, usage analytics, and business impact
Create new content that supports common use cases and demonstrates the impact of Depot in real-world CI environments
Support product launches with technical content that explains what changed and why it matters
Help engineers ship more by writing the things they don’t have time to
Build and own Depot's technical content strategy as the company scales
Skills & Experience
Strong technical writer with experience creating content for a developer audience
Experience with containerization, CI/CD pipelines, or build tooling preferred
Comfortable working from source code, changelogs, and internal notes
Prioritizes clarity and usefulness above style
Writes with authority, accuracy, and developer empathy
Self-motivated and able to find and execute on high-leverage content opportunities without waiting for prompts
Depot values and culture
We are a fully remote and globally distributed team across the US, Europe, and Canada. As a startup focused on iteration speed and technical depth, we care deeply about how people work together.
We look for self starters.
Part of working in a startup is being able to self navigate the ambiguity and take meaningful action to keep the momentum moving forward. There is no shortage of fun, hard, interesting things to work on, but you need to be self motivated to pick them up and go.
We’re transparent.
We do not hide how the business is doing or what the tradeoffs are. Internally and externally, we tell the truth about how things work and where they break.
We’re data driven.
We track performance to the second. We ship benchmarks with methodology. A decision without data is just a theory.
We’re relentlessly helpful.
We meet developers where they are and help them move faster. Inside the company, we take the same approach with each other.
We do more with less.
We maximize impact through efficiency and resourcefulness. We value folks who can ruthlessly prioritize and take action. Constraints drive innovation, not limitation.
We’re not your family.
We’re a team. We expect you to get things done and contribute meaningfully, and also to protect your time, rest, and personal life. Balance matters.
About
Depot
Depot is a build acceleration and developer productivity platform that saves companies like PostHog, Wistia, Semgrep, and Secoda thousands of hours in build time every week.
We are developers. We started Depot because we were frustrated with the constant pain of slow build performance. We were fed up waiting for builds and annoyed by the lack of tooling and providers that actually made builds performant. So, we went and built the solution we had always wanted.
Slow builds are the dam standing in the way between mediocrity and innovation. They’re wasteful, expensive, and a drain on developer happiness & productivity. They slow down innovation.
Taking a 40-minute build down to a minute, changes everything. We help folks save literal years in build time every single week.
And we’re just getting started. For us, it’s all about iteration speed and keeping developers in their flow state.
Our mission is to be relentless in accelerating software development.

data.title: When Is WebAssembly Going to Get DOM Support?
data.author: jazzypants
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了WebAssembly (Wasm) 是否能直接支持DOM操作，并指出Wasm可能永远不会直接访问DOM，但通过JavaScript间接调用DOM API已经足够成熟，适用于各种Web应用。Wasm与JavaScript严格分离，但通过“粘合代码”可以实现与JavaScript API的无缝集成。文章通过示例展示了如何利用JavaScript作为中介，让Wasm调用如`console.log`这样的Web API。Wasm模块通过导入和导出功能与JavaScript交互，且使用数组和整数索引来处理JavaScript对象引用。尽管未来可能引入直接调用Web API的机制，但目前的方案已能有效减少代码量并提升性能。Wasm与JavaScript的集成仍在不断发展中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebAssembly（WASM）的应用、与DOM交互的挑战以及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• **支持WASM与DOM交互的复杂性**：[sfvisser] 指出，在Rust和TypeScript之间通过WASM进行交互的层非常痛苦，需要大量缓慢且不安全的胶水代码。虽然WASM允许后端和前端共享逻辑，但频繁跨越边界交互并不理想。

• **WASM的潜力未被充分实现**：[apatheticonion] 认为WASM本应 revolutionize 网页开发，但多年来其应用仍限于单一线程的 niche 用例，未能充分发挥潜力。

• **性能问题和浏览器差异**：[evrimoztamur] 提到在iOS的WebKit/Safari上运行WASM图形应用时性能损失严重，而在其他浏览器上表现良好，强调了跨浏览器性能问题。

• **对WASM进展的失望与期望**：[jauntywundrkind] 表示对WASM进展缓慢感到失望，期待更多更新和明确的未来规划。虽然有进展但仍不清楚如何有效整合WASM。

• **对开源能力的担忧**：[CaptainFever] 担心WASM的广泛使用会导致网页的源代码不再默认可见，影响透明性。

• **替代方案的建议**：[gchamonlive] 提出可以通过类似Phoenix LiveView的消息传递机制来减少DOM操作的复杂性。

• **DOM访问的编码问题**：[theSherwood] 不希望WASM依赖UTF-16编码进行DOM访问，建议引入8位编码的DOMString8接口。

• **对WASM理解的困惑**：[MisterTea] 对WASM是否应理解DOM提出疑问，认为WASM不应直接与DOM交互，除非有人编写相关代码。

• **现代WASM的进展和组件模型**：[hardwaresofton] 提到Bytecode Alliance正在推进现代WASM的DOM交互支持，尽管实验性的浏览器shim仍未完善，但已有一些支持可用。

• **对DOM支持的反对意见**：[lucideer] 认为WASM增加DOM支持会带来复杂性和安全问题，不认为其必要性足够显著。

• **对简化胶水代码的需求**：[jagged-chisel] 强调需要简化与JS API互操作的胶水代码，建议允许列出WASM将调用的JS函数以减少手工编写。

• **DOM wrapper的需求**：[edg5000] 询问是否有人为C++/Rust编写了匹配JavaScript API的DOM wrapper，以便在C++/Rust应用中操作DOM。

• **在WASM中实现DOM的建议**：[amelius] 提出可以在WASM中实现DOM，以彻底解决DOM兼容性问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应让WASM直接支持DOM操作以及如何简化WASM与JS的交互。
• 讨论中多次提到性能问题，特别是跨浏览器的一致性。
• 对现代WASM和组件模型的更新进展有一些积极的期望和建议。
• 部分评论者对WASM的未来感到困惑和失望，期待更明确的路线图和简化开发的方案。

Past Issues

July 2, 2025
Volume 23, issue 3
PDF
When Is WebAssembly Going to Get DOM Support?
Or, how I learned to stop worrying and love glue code
Daniel Ehrenberg
Is WebAssembly (Wasm) really ready for production usage in web applications, even though that usage requires integration with a web page and the APIs used to manipulate it, such as the DOM?
Simultaneously, the answer to this question is that "Wasm might never get
direct
DOM access,"
and
"Yes, Wasm is ready for all kinds of web-integrated uses, having supported calling out to the DOM (with a little indirection) since day zero." Let me explain.
WebAssembly was designed from its outset to have a strict separation from JavaScript. Unlike
asm.js
(developer.mozilla.org), which is unavoidably embedded in JavaScript, the core Wasm bytecode format is completely clean of all the "legacy" of JavaScript. At the same time, it says it right in the name—Wasm is part of the web platform. So, why are web APIs like the DOM still tied to JavaScript, and why are there no new Wasm versions?
The answer is that new versions of web APIs, such as the DOM, are not needed to make them usable from Wasm; the existing JavaScript APIs work just fine. When used in the browser or other JavaScript environments, Wasm includes various JavaScript APIs that allow compiler-generated glue code to provide seamless access to any JavaScript code.
WebAssembly has been progressively evolving toward allowing build toolchains to emit less code, specifically less JavaScript. These improvements target the code that makes real web applications slow and bulky in Wasm. Wasm's integration with JavaScript will continue to evolve and deepen through the work of the W3C Wasm CG (Community Group).
Maybe, if it turns out to cause performance and code-size improvements to justify its complexity, a mechanism could be added in the future to call web APIs straight from Wasm, but this mechanism would require tremendous effort to design and implement. On the other hand, a bit of JavaScript glue to connect web APIs might not be
the
bottleneck to worry about, especially when there are other sources of overhead to address.
Gluing Wasm to JavaScript
To understand how Wasm and JavaScript fit together, let's work through an example adapted from
Wasm's excellent documentation on MDN
(developer.mozilla.org) showing how Wasm can call
console.log
. Though Wasm's main format is a binary bytecode, the specification also defines a text format called WAT (Wasm text) that makes it easy to see what's going on:
(module
(func $log (
import
"myConsole" "myLog"
) (param i32))
(func (
export
"log42"
)
i32.
const
42
call $log))
Wasm is a module language: Each Wasm module declares imports and exports. To run a module, you
instantiate
it with a set of imports, and this operation provides the set of exports. The Wasm JavaScript API makes this module instantiation functionality accessible from JavaScript.
This example is a simple module that imports a function called
myLog
from the module
myConsole
. It exports a function
log42
that calls that function with the argument
42
. JavaScript code can call any web API by referencing the global object, but Wasm has access only to what you give it, so
console.log
is threaded through to Wasm through a module import:
const
importObject = {
myConsole: {
myLog(arg) {
console.log(arg);
}
}
};
const
{ instance } =
await
WebAssembly
.instantiateStreaming(
fetch(
"simple.wasm"
), importObject);
instance.exports.log42();
The idea is that build toolchains that output Wasm for websites will actually output a combination of Wasm and JavaScript, with the latter responsible for loading the module and linking it with the appropriate JavaScript capabilities, such as this
myConsole
module.
Modeling Everything with Flat Memory
To paraphrase German mathematician Leopold Kronecker, God created
i32
,
i64
,
f32
, and
f64
; all the rest is the work of man.
WebAssembly started with a simple built-in type system. As far as values that can live on the stack and be passed as arguments to functions, it initially supported just what would fit in its flat, bitmapped memory: the four byte-addressable numeric types just mentioned. It turns out, however, that this gives Wasm bytecode full flexibility to call JavaScript APIs, even those that take objects as arguments, rather than just numbers as in the
console.log
example.
Here's how you do it:
Maintain an array in JavaScript that contains all of the references to the JavaScript objects the Wasm program needs to concern itself with.
The modules that JavaScript exports to Wasm are wrapped. When a function is expected to take an object as an argument and return a different object, the wrapper will accept and return integer indices into that array, allocating a new entry for the return value.
Wasm code will explicitly free these references when it no longer needs them by calling another function imported from JavaScript that manages a free list.

主要讨论点：生物医学领域中高质量数据集的创建、标注、开放性及相关工作机会

不同观点：
• **panabee** 认为，生物医学领域的数据集常包含不准确的数据，因为缺乏对准确性的激励，且合格的标注者稀缺。他们付费给斯坦福的医学博士来标注新的问题，并计划将数据集开源。panabee 强调了医疗数据准确性的重要性，因为过时或错误的信息可能导致临床错误。同时提到医学知识变化快速，可能使训练数据失效。

• **vidarh** 分享了自己在数据标注和审核方面的工作经验，指出该领域存在工作层次结构，大部分工作由低成本标注者完成，而高难度任务则由较高层次的专家处理。他还提到，尽管有些人能获得高薪，但整体上薪酬并不如外界想象的那么高。vidarh 也提到了工具的改进，如利用合成数据来减少专家工作量。

• **TheAceOfHearts** 建议将这些数据集开放给公众使用，以避免重复劳动和资源浪费，并指出目前很多公司将数据集视为竞争壁垒，限制了创新。

• **joshdavham** 提到自己被一家公司联系去做高质数据集的标注工作，但因招聘方式不当（通过GitHub获取邮件）而拒绝了邀请，并认为这种招聘方式不道德。

• **techterrier** 将当前的数据标注工作与过去的工作外包趋势相比较，认为现在人们是在教机器人取代自己的工作。

• **TrackerFF** 提到自己在数据标注和数据质量保证领域的冷接触招聘增多，反映出该领域需求的增长。

• **rnxrx** 预测私营企业将通过标记和出售“无用”的数据集来获利，这对传统企业的价值评估可能有重要影响。

• **the_brin92** 分享了自己在数据标注项目中的经验，指出项目复杂性增加和模型仍存在许多问题，且认为人文背景在判断AI模型响应质量方面有优势。

• **SoftTalker** 引用了“苦涩的教训”一文，质疑当前依赖大规模数据集的趋势，认为可能忽视了更基本的AI原则。

• **quantum_state** 认为这是专家系统的演变。

• **cryptokush** 幽默地称这是“宏观数据精炼”的开始。

• **verisimi** 讽刺地指出，通过AI生成大量低质内容（如Reddit评论、假数据集）可能是应对AI接管的办法。

• **charlieyu1** 对开放数据集和专家团队的未来持怀疑态度，提到一家AI公司去年因成本问题解散了专家团队。

• **Melonololoti** 认为AI不仅仅是炒作，已经开始实际利用大量数据，且这个过程不会很快停止，强调了通过人类反馈（如点赞/点差）训练AI的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 数据集的开放性与商业壁垒：有些人认为开放数据集能促进创新，而另一些人认为数据集是企业的竞争壁垒。
• 数据标注工作的薪酬和招聘方式：有人指出高薪机会存在，但整体薪酬结构不平衡，且招聘方式有时不道德。
• 数据质量和准确性：在医疗AI领域，数据的准确性和及时性被认为是至关重要的，错误数据可能导致严重后果。
• AI模型训练中的数据问题：讨论了数据集过时和错误信息对AI模型的影响，以及医学知识变化对数据集的挑战。
• 专家在数据标注中的角色：专家在数据标注和审核中的作用被强调，但也有人质疑高成本的专家团队是否可持续。

争议焦点：
• 数据集的开放与商业化：有人主张开放数据集以促进创新，而另一些人认为数据集是企业的竞争壁垒，限制了创新。
• 数据标注工作的薪酬：有人获得了较高的薪酬，但整体薪酬水平并不高，且存在招聘方式不道德的现象。

data.title: SubTropolis and KC's Limestone Caves
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 《SubTropolis与堪萨斯城石灰岩洞穴的故事》一文介绍了位于堪萨斯城地下的全球最大地下商业综合体——SubTropolis。这个占地超过600万平方英尺的地下城建于2.7亿年历史的石灰岩矿床中，最初是20世纪40年代开采石灰岩的矿场，后由堪萨斯城酋长队创始人拉马尔·亨特在60年代将其转型为商业综合体。SubTropolis因其恒定的温度（65-70华氏度）和自然气候控制环境，吸引了福特汽车、Pillsbury和美国邮政等大公司入驻，用于存储车辆、电影胶片和档案等。该地下城拥有超过10英里的铺设道路和高效节能的LED照明，并因其天然的隔热性能获得ENERGY STAR®100%评级。目前，SubTropolis正计划扩建800万平方英尺的工业空间，展示出其持续发展的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：石灰岩和混凝土的强度比较

不同观点：
• **mrbluecoat** 提出疑问，根据某个信息来源，石灰岩柱的强度是混凝土的六倍，质疑石灰岩是否真的比混凝土更强。
• **user123** 认为石灰岩的强度可能在特定情况下超过混凝土，但强调混凝土的强度取决于混合比例和使用环境。认为简单比较不够全面，需要考虑具体施工条件和材料配方。
• **buildingexpert87** 指出，石灰岩作为天然材料，其强度变异性较大，而混凝土可以通过工程设计调整强度。提出混凝土的现代配方可以达到甚至超过天然石灰岩的强度，特别是在受压情况下。

补充讨论：
• **realstoneadvocate** 提到石灰岩的耐久性和抗压能力在某些古老建筑中已经得到验证，比如在古隧道和建筑基础中。认为天然石材有其独特的优势，尤其是在抗风化方面。
• **techbuilder** 则指出，虽然石灰岩在某些案例中表现出色，但混凝土的广泛应用和可调性使其成为现代建筑的首选材料。并提到在实际工程中，选择材料不仅仅看强度，还要考虑成本、可获得性和施工便捷性。

争议焦点：石灰岩和混凝土的强度对比，特别是在实际应用中的表现。一方强调天然石灰岩的优越性，另一方则认为混凝土的工程可调性和广泛适用性更具优势。

44632218.article_content:
The Story of SubTropolis & KC’s Limestone Caves
Aug 22
Written By
KCYesterday
Beneath Kansas City's streets lies an unexpected wonder—
SubTropolis
, the world's largest underground business complex, spanning over 6 million square feet in a 270-million-year-old limestone deposit.
Carved out of limestone in the 1940s, this hidden metropolis was the vision of Lamar Hunt, famed founder of the Kansas City Chiefs. Originally a mining site, SubTropolis has become an essential part of Kansas City’s economic landscape.
The origins of SubTropolis date back to the late 19th and early 20th centuries, when extensive limestone mining operations supported Kansas City's rapid expansion. When demand for limestone dwindled, the vast network of tunnels left behind presented a unique opportunity.
Recognizing the potential of these naturally climate-controlled spaces, Hunt transformed the old mines into a modern underground city, officially opening SubTropolis in the 1960s.
Courtesy Hunt Midwest
SubTropolis quickly attracted a range of tenants, including major companies like Ford Motors, Pillsbury, and Russell Stover. Ford, for instance, uses the underground space to store vehicles and customize truck beds in a controlled environment. In the early 1970s,
​Ford leased 25 acres of underground space​
to store thousands of unsold vehicles until they could be sold.
The stable temperature of 65 to 70 degrees Fahrenheit makes it ideal for preserving delicate items, such as original film reels of Hollywood classics like "Gone with the Wind" and "The Wizard of Oz," stored deep within SubTropolis. The US Postal Service and the National Archives also lease space in the naturally climate controlled space.
Courtesy
​YouTube​
/ Great Big Story.
Covering an area large enough to fit 42 Arrowhead Stadiums, SubTropolis is a marvel of modern engineering. Over 10 miles of paved roads crisscross its tunnels, well-lit by energy-efficient LED lights.
The limestone walls act as natural insulators, significantly reducing the need for heating and cooling, earning SubTropolis a perfect 100 percent rating from ENERGY STAR®.
Safety and security are paramount in SubTropolis. The limestone pillars supporting the tunnels are six times stronger than concrete, making the complex one of the safest places to be during natural disasters. Security measures include 24/7 surveillance and commissioned officers, essential for the government agencies and high-value tenants housed within the complex.
As SubTropolis continues to evolve, plans for expansion are already underway, with another 8 million square feet of industrial space set to be developed.
What began as an abandoned limestone mine has become a thriving underground city, a testament to Lamar Hunt's ingenuity and resilience.

data.title: Fourier lightfield multiview stereoscope for large field-of-view 3D imaging
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为FiLM-Scope的成像设备，结合了傅里叶光场显微术和多视角立体成像技术，能够捕捉大视场的高分辨率3D视频。该设备由48个微型摄像头组成，放置在高通量主镜头后面，可同时捕捉48张12.8兆像素的图像，视场范围为28×37毫米，角度范围为21度×29度，横向分辨率达到22微米。文章还介绍了一种自监督算法，用于从这些图像中重建3D高度图，高度精度达到11微米。实验展示了该系统在工具跟踪和人体皮肤3D变形可视化中的应用，视频捕捉速度高达每秒100帧。FiLM-Scope有潜力在多种显微手术环境中改善3D可视化效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对演示的评价及工具追踪逻辑的建议

不同观点：
• Pedro_Caetano认为演示非常酷，并对整体演示给予积极评价。他指出，当前的演示存在"infinite depth"视线伪影的问题，这可能是由于手术工具的追踪不够精确所致。
• Pedro_Caetano进一步提出改进建议，建议通过增加工具追踪逻辑来解决视线伪影问题，从而提升演示的精度和实用性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了演示中一个具体的技术问题，即手术工具的"infinite depth"视线伪影，这表明在工具的视觉呈现上可能存在深度感知不准确的情况。
• Pedro_Caetano的建议显示出对技术细节的关注，特别是通过优化工具追踪逻辑来改善演示效果，这可能涉及到计算机视觉或增强现实技术的进一步应用。
• 争议焦点可能在于是否值得为了解决视线伪影问题而增加额外的工具追踪逻辑，因为这可能会增加系统的复杂性和开发成本。

We present the Fourier lightfield multiview stereoscope (FiLM-Scope). This imaging device combines concepts from Fourier lightfield microscopy and multiview stereo imaging to capture high-resolution 3D videos over large fields of view. data.title: Project Lyra – Exploring Interstellar Objects
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary:
Project Lyra旨在利用现有和近期技术，设计探测星际物体如1I/'Oumuamua和2I/Borisov的航天器任务。1I/'Oumuamua是2017年由夏威夷Pan-STARRS 1望远镜发现的星际小行星，其速度为26 km/s，正在离开太阳系。2019年发现了第二颗星际物体2I/Borisov，这是一颗彗星。由于这些物体是星际物质的近距离样本，科学价值极高。然而，由于1I/'Oumuamua正迅速离开太阳系，追赶它是一大技术挑战。

Project Lyra团队初步研究显示，利用现有技术（如Falcon Heavy或Space Launch System发射器、固体火箭发动机和Parker Solar Probe热盾），可在2021年发射探测器，但时间过于紧迫。因此，团队继续研究2024年后的发射机会，以确保有足够时间开发专用航天器。这些研究结果已发表在arXiv和Acta Astronautica期刊上。

Project Lyra – Exploring Interstellar Objects
Project Lyra develops concepts for reaching interstellar objects such as 1I / 'Oumuamua and 2I / Borisov with a spacecraft, based on near-term technologies. But what is an interstellar object?
Laser sail spacecraft arriving at 'Oumuamua, the interstellar asteroid (Credit: Maciej Rebisz)
What is 1I/'Oumuamua and what is an Interstellar Object?
On October 19th 2017, the University of Hawaii’s Pan-STARRS 1 telescope on Haleakala discovered a fast-moving object near the Earth, initially named A/2017 U1. It is now designated as 1I/’Oumuamua. This object was found to be not bound to the solar system. It has a velocity at infinity of ~26 km/s and an incoming radiant (direction of motion) near the solar apex in the constellation Lyra. Due to the non-observation of a tail in the proximity of the Sun, the object does not seem to be a comet but an asteroid. More recent observations from the Palomar Observatory indicate that the object is reddish, similar to Kuiper belt objects. This is a sign of space weathering.
Discovery of the Second Interstellar Object, 2I/Borisov and Spacecraft Missions
When will such an object visit us again? End of 2019, a second interstellar object, 2I/Borisov was discovered, which is a comet. As 1I/‘Oumuamua and 2I/Borisov are the nearest macroscopic samples of interstellar material, the scientific returns from sampling the object are hard to overstate. Detailed study of interstellar materials at interstellar distances are likely decades away, even if Breakthrough Initiatives’ Project Starshot, for example, is vigorously pursued. Hence, an interesting question is if there is a way to exploit this unique opportunity by sending a spacecraft to 1I/’Oumuamua to make observations at close range.
Project Lyra and the Initiative for Interstellar Studies
Logo for Project Lyra
To answer these questions, the Initiative for Interstellar Studies, i4is, announced Project Lyra on the 30
th
October 2017. The goal of the project is to assess the feasibility of a mission to 1I/’Oumuamua, 2I/Borisov and other potential interstellar objects, using current and near-term technology and to propose mission concepts for achieving a fly-by or rendezvous. The challenge is formidable: 1I/’Oumuamua has a hyperbolic excess velocity of 26 km/s, which translates to a velocity of 5.5 AU/year. It will be beyond Saturn’s orbit within two years. This is much faster than any object humanity has ever launched into space. Compare this to Voyager 1, the fastest object humanity has ever built, which has a hyperbolic excess velocity of 16.6 km/s. As 1I/’Oumuamua is already on its way of leaving our solar system, any spacecraft launched in the future needs to chase it. The challenge to reach the object could stretch the current technological envelope of space exploration.
Initial Expiditous Results of Project Lyra
After days of intense work, we (i.e. Andreas M. Hein, Nikolaos Perakis, Kelvin F. Long, Adam Crowl, Marshall Eubanks, Robert G. Kennedy III & Richard Osborne) have published some preliminary results on the 8
th
November 2017 for reaching the object within a timeframe of a few decades. The paper was published on arXiv and can be accessed
here
. Subsequently, our arXiv paper created a surge of media articles, which can be found below. It was a month or so later, on 15
th
December 2017, after these results were published, that the Project Lyra team was contacted by Adam Hibberd who appraised the team (via Andreas Hein) of the findings of his research. This analysis exploited his recent software development,
'Optimum Interplanetary Trajectory Software' (OITS
)
. His discoveries using OITS were then incorporated into the paper and a revised version of the paper
"Project Lyra: Sending a spacecraft to 1I/’Oumuamua (former A/2017 U1), the interstellar asteroid"
was eventually accepted by the journal Acta Astronautica and was published on the 7th of January 2019 (find
here for arXiv preprint
and
here
for Acta version).
In the paper, we demonstrate that missions to 'Oumuamua are feasible with current and near-term technologies (Falcon Heavy or Space Launch System launcher, solid rocket motors, and Parker Solar probe heat shield), with an optimal launch date in 2021. However, this launch date would be too soon for developing a dedicated spacecraft, something that usually takes 5 to 10 years for an interplanetary mission.

after 2024

data.title: NPM stylus package contained malicious code and was removed from the registry
data.author: vandot
data.article_summary: `stylus` 0.0.1-security 版本因包含恶意代码，已被 npm 安全团队从注册表中移除。为防止用户受影响，发布了一个占位包。更多信息可访问 npmjs 网站查询。该版本有 2277 个依赖项，每周下载量超过 360 万。目前无许可证，包大小为 418 字节，包含 2 个文件。用户需谨慎对待此恶意软件警告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NPM中stylus包的安全问题及其引发的争议和处理方法

不同观点：
• sensanaty认为NPM工具在处理stylus包的安全问题时存在漏洞，尤其是`npm audit`和相关命令未能检测到lockfile中明显存在的安全问题，这让他感到困惑和不安。
• righthand对NPM整个生态系统表示不满，认为NPM在包管理方面存在严重的安全问题，特别是在升级包和处理安全漏洞时耗费了大量时间，并且`npm audit fix`命令经常不能正确修复问题，甚至会降级包的版本。
• maury91关注stylus包是否被实际入侵，引用了GitHub上的安全建议链接，并推测可能是stylus的维护者账户被入侵，导致多个相关包受到影响。
• yoavfr和kontercola提供了临时的解决方案，即在package.json中使用overrides字段强制指定stylus版本以绕过问题。
• dmitryeu进一步补充，建议直接从GitHub安装stylus包，并提供了相关链接，指出维护者正在与NPM官方交涉以解决问题。
• bapak对事件的描述提出异议，认为没有证据表明stylus包本身被入侵，NPM可能是为了安全起见下架了与某可疑维护者相关的所有包，而不只是特定版本。
• kaelwd指出，NPM通常只会下架特定被入侵的版本，而不是整个包，因此这次事件有些不寻常。
• finchisko怀疑GitHub上的安全建议数据库可能遭到攻击，因为在近期出现了大量类似的恶意软件报告。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于stylus包是否确实被入侵，以及NPM和GitHub在处理安全问题时的透明度和准确性。
• 多个用户提供了绕过该问题的具体方法，表明社区在问题解决前的自发应对措施。
• 对NPM生态系统的整体可靠性存在质疑，尤其是其包管理和安全审计工具的有效性。
