Many cities face the following problem. They have railway lines that go where people live. But these railway lines end at the edge of the city center, and don’t go out the other side.
For cities with this problem, the solution is
through running
. Terminating a train and turning it around takes a lot of space, space that is usually unavailable in a city center. This means running a railway line through the city often doubles or triples the number of trains it can handle. As a bonus, passengers who are going from one side of the city to the other can do that much more quickly, with no change.
Many cities, such as London, Paris, Munich and Milan, have used through running to turn some of their existing Victorian railway lines into metro-style services, by building tunnels under the city center. A few other cities, like Berlin, built viaducts (bridges that carry roads and railways over obstacles), while others, such as Cologne, have simply added platforms at their main stations to enable suburban trains to run through. But all of these are big cities, with over a million people, where the property value uplift or extra revenues from fares can cover
the enormous costs
of tunneling. But there is another option, affordable for smaller cities or large towns: the
tram-train
.
A Karlsruhe tram, running on railway tracks. Image credit:
Baden-Wuerttemberg
.
Karlsruhe is a small city of only 300,000 people in southwestern Germany, near the French border. The city’s main station is nearly two kilometers from the city center, following a project in the early twentieth century to build a larger station on a less cramped site. This caused great inconvenience to passengers, who had to change to the city’s tram network in order to get to the old center.
In 1957, the city took the first steps towards creating a new type of transit, the tram-train, when it took over a bankrupt suburban railway, the Albtalbahn, and extended it into the city center over the tram network.
Over the next four years the line’s gauge (the space between the rails) was converted from 1,000 millimeters to 1,435 millimeters, the standard gauge used by the tram network, and it was re-electrified at the same voltage as the tramway. The modernization of the line enabled quicker journey times – the 70 minute journey to Bad Herrenalb, the line’s terminus, was reduced to 46 minutes – but more importantly passengers who wanted to get to the city center did not need to change to a tram.
The idea of a tram that runs outside of a city’s urban area was not new: Vienna, for instance, had been operating a similar line to the neighboring spa town of Baden since 1907. Karlsruhe’s inventive step, which came later, was to extend the tram-train onto railway lines that did not just carry tram traffic. In 1979, the line was extended onto a freight railway north of the city, and in 1992 the first tram-train took over pre-existing passenger services, to the town of Bretten.
Joining the tram and train networks together was
tricky
. German railways are electrified at 15 kilovolts alternating current, while Karlsruhe’s trams use 750 volt direct current, which meant that the city needed to procure trams capable of using both voltages, which were (and still are) rare. The railway and the tram network used two different signaling systems, the ‘traffic lights’ that are used to control the movement of rail traffic. The trams have to use
retractable steps
to overcome the big gap between the 2.65 meter-wide trams and platforms which can handle 3 meter-wide trains. These steps also enable later models of the trams, whose floors are 570 millimeters above the ground, to work with both 380 and 760 millimeter-high platforms.
Overcoming these technical problems led to a much better network.
Ridership of the Bretten line went up 400 percent
after it was extended into the city center on tramlines, and the line now has
18,000 trips per day
, up from 2,000 before the tram-train took over. Passenger numbers on the network
doubled
between 1985 and 1999, after several more lines had been added. The network today, which carries
170 million passengers
per year, is over 660 kilometers long, longer than the combined length of Munich’s tram, metro and suburban railway networks.
Karlruhe’s transit system. Image credit:
Wikimedia Commons.
Tram-trains have trade-offs. Trams are
slower than trains
, because they have to share road space with cars, pedestrians and bicycles. Where possible, therefore, Karls

data.title: Show HN: Self-updating MCP server for official pip, uv, poetry and conda docs
data.author: keminghe
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个自更新的MCP服务器，用于官方pip、uv、poetry和conda文档，通过Docker实现自动化每周更新，减少开发者在VSCode或Cursor中使用AI助手时的维护负担。主要功能包括通过Docker拉取最新镜像并配置到IDE中，开发者可以查询官方文档。项目包含自动更新架构，每周同步官方文档并重建搜索索引，自动发布最新Docker镜像。此外，项目提供贡献指南和未来计划，如支持更多依赖管理工具和增加文件格式索引。项目采用MIT许可，并通过GitHub处理问题和功能请求。
data.comments_summary:

• mrbonner：认为演示虽然帮助不大，但引发了其对编码代理文档优化的思考。他质疑当前基于RAG（检索增强生成）的方法是否为最佳解决方案，暗示可能有更好的技术路径。

• dcreater：提出演示可能已经被Context7（一种新的技术或工具）所取代，暗示当前讨论的技术或演示可能已经过时。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对当前技术方案（RAG）的批评与反思，mrbonner认为RAG并非最优解，可能有其他更好的方法来实现编码代理的文档优化。
• 对演示任务的实际应用价值存在争议，WhatsName认为该任务不具代表性，无法体现工具的真实能力。

data.title: Migrating a ZFS Pool from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者如何在不将数据转移到外部存储的情况下，将家用TrueNAS服务器从RAIDZ1迁移到RAIDZ2，同时仅增加了三块8TB硬盘。具体步骤如下：

1. **初始状态**：作者有一个4x8TB的RAIDZ1 ZFS存储池，使用了18TB容量。
2. **借用一块硬盘创建RAIDZ2池**：移除一块原RAIDZ1硬盘，用三块新硬盘和一块8TB的稀疏文件创建新的RAIDZ2池。
3. **下线稀疏文件**：将稀疏文件下线，RAIDZ2池依然健康。
4. **迁移快照**：将RAIDZ1池的快照通过`zfs send`迁移到RAIDZ2池。
5. **销毁旧池**：确认数据迁移成功后，销毁旧的RAIDZ1池。
6. **替换稀疏文件并扩展新池**：用旧池的一块硬盘替换稀疏文件，然后通过ZFS扩展功能将剩余的旧硬盘加入新池。

作者选择RAIDZ2是因为它可以容忍两块硬盘故障，而ZFS不支持直接从RAIDZ1转换为RAIDZ2，因此作者采用了上述方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对数据冗余和磁盘操作的实现方式存在不同看法，尤其是RAIDZ1和RAIDZ2的应用。

不同观点：
• **xmodem的观点**：
  - 最初对能够在不使用外部存储的情况下，仅通过添加三块额外的8TB磁盘完成数据迁移表示赞赏，并认为这是一种简洁的解决方案。
  - 然而，在了解具体操作步骤后（特别是需要先借用一个磁盘来创建RAIDZ2池，且原RAIDZ1池会处于降级状态），对该方法表示失望。
  - 认为这种操作并没有真正提供一种安全、冗余的数据迁移方式，反而会使原系统进入不安全的状态（降级的RAIDZ1池）。

• **mtlynch的观点**：
  - 作为文章作者，对提出的方案持积极态度，并愿意接受提问和反馈。
  - 虽然没有直接反驳xmodem的质疑，但似乎愿意进一步解释或澄清自己的方法。

补充讨论：

44659676.article_content:
I recently upgraded my home TrueNAS server and migrated 18 TB of data from a 4-disk RAIDZ1 ZFS pool to a new RAIDZ2 pool.
The neat part is that I did it with only three additional 8 TB disks and never transferred my data to external storage.
Upgrading from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2 without moving data to external storage is tricky because:
You can’t convert a RAIDZ1 pool to a RAIDZ2 pool in place.
You can’t shrink a ZFS pool to a smaller number of disks.
You can’t fit 18 TB of data on a 3-disk, 8TB RAIDZ2 pool (the three new disks).
How I did it
🔗︎
Step 0: Initial state
🔗︎
Starting out, I have a 4x8TB RAIDZ1 ZFS pool, and I’m using 18 TB of its 23 TB capacity. I purchased three refurbished 8 TB disks for this migration.
Step 1: Borrow one disk to create a RAIDZ2 pool
🔗︎
To begin, I remove one disk from my original RAIDZ1 pool, leaving it in a degraded state.
I then create a new 5x8TB RAIDZ2 pool using:
My three new disks
One disk from my RAIDZ1 pool
One 8 TB sparse file to act as a fake disk
The sparse file is in my
/tmp
directory, even though the filesystem there can’t actually store 8 TB of data. That’s okay because the sparse file is only temporary. It’s a hack that allows me to create a 5-disk pool, but I won’t write any data to it.
Step 2: Offline the fake disk
🔗︎
Next, I offline the fake disk (the 8 TB sparse file) from the RAIDZ2 pool.
After offlining the fake disk, the pool is still healthy, as RAIDZ2 can operate with two disks missing.
Step 3: Migrate a snapshot of the RAIDZ1 pool to the RAIDZ2 pool
🔗︎
I snapshot all datasets in my RAIDZ1 pool and migrate the snapshot to my new RAIDZ2 pool using
zfs send
.
Step 4: Destroy the old pool
🔗︎
Once I verify that I’ve successfully migrated my data to the RAIDZ2 pool, I destroy my old RAIDZ1 pool, leaving me with three extra disks.
Step 5: Replace the fake disk with an old disk
🔗︎
I use one disk from my old RAIDZ1 pool to replace the fake disk in my RAIDZ2 pool, so it is no longer missing a disk.
Step 6: Expand the new pool with the old disks
🔗︎
Finally, I use ZFS expansion to add the last two disks from my old RAIDZ1 pool to my new RAIDZ2 pool, giving me a total of 33 TB of usable storage on a healthy 7x8TB RAIDZ2 pool.
Why switch from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2?
🔗︎
I built my
home TrueNAS server in 2022
with a 4x8TB RAIDZ1 pool. I was comfortable with RAIDZ1 because it could tolerate one disk failure, and I considered it unlikely for two out of my four disks to fail simultaneously.
What I failed to consider was when I add disks to the pool, each new disk increases my odds of data loss. I’m not worried about two disks failing out of four, but if I have six or eight disks, then concurrent failures begin to feel more likely.
Every disk I add to my RAIDZ1 pool makes a migration to RAIDZ2 harder because it means my new pool has to be even bigger, and I have even fewer physical disk slots available to a new pool.
RAIDZ2 can tolerate two disk failures without data loss. Even if I expanded to 10 disks (the max capacity of my current server chassis), three simultaneous disk failures feels unlikely enough that I’m not worried.
Why is switching from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2 hard?
🔗︎
ZFS doesn’t support switching from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2. You set the RAIDZ mode at pool creation time and can never change it.
The naïve solution would be to buy five extra disks, build a RAIDZ2 pool, then move all of my data over to the new pool. That would leave me with 4 original disks + 5 new disks = 9 total disks when I only wanted 6-7.
If you search online for how to convert a RAIDZ1 pool to RAIDZ2, everyone says to do it the naïve way or to move all your data to a spare ZFS server, destroy your RAIDZ1 pool, create a RAIDZ2 pool in its place, then migrate your data back. But what you’re like me and don’t have a spare 18 TB ZFS server lying around in one of your yachts?
The reason there isn’t much guidance on a more efficient way to switch from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2 is that my solution depends on
RAIDZ expansion
, which only became available in ZFS
six months ago
.
Migrating from RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2: in practice
🔗︎
In theory, my RAIDZ1 to RAIDZ2 migration plan was straightforward, but I ran into a few hiccups actually performing this migration.
I’m sharing a detailed journal of the exact commands and output for anyone who wants to repeat this process.
Step 1: A practice migration with USB sticks
🔗︎
My migration plan involves some risky maneuvers. Before I tried it on my main TrueNAS server with all of my data, I first tried it on a test server.
I installed TrueNAS Core 25.04 on an old mini PC and then connected 7 USB thumbdrives.
Testing my migration strategy on a spare TrueNAS server and seven USB thumbdrives
It wasn’t a perfect experiment because the drives were different sizes, but the process worked. It gave me confidence to try my migration plan on my production server.
Step 2: Backing up my data
🔗︎
I said above that I never moved my data to external storage, but that’s not strictly true. I did use external storage

1. **初始状态**：作者有一个4x8TB的RAIDZ1 ZFS存储池，使用了18TB容量。
2. **借用一块硬盘创建RAIDZ2池**：移除一块原RAIDZ1硬盘，用三块新硬盘和一块8TB的稀疏文件创建新的RAIDZ2池。

4. **迁移快照**：将RAIDZ1池的快照通过`zfs send`迁移到RAIDZ2池。
5. **销毁旧池**：确认数据迁移成功后，销毁旧的RAIDZ1池。
6. **替换稀疏文件并扩展新池**：用旧池的一块硬盘替换稀疏文件，然后通过ZFS扩展功能将剩余的旧硬盘加入新池。

作者选择RAIDZ2是因为它可以容忍两块硬盘故障，而ZFS不支持直接从RAIDZ1转换为RAIDZ2，因此作者采用了上述方法。

data.article_summary: 美国正致力于在全球人工智能（AI）领域取得主导地位，以促进经济繁荣、国家安全和科技创新。特朗普总统在其第二任期初期提出了《美国AI行动计划》，该计划基于三大支柱：加速AI创新、建设AI基础设施、以及在国际外交和安全领域引领AI发展。第一支柱侧重于通过私营部门推动AI创新，减少监管障碍，促进开放源代码和技术采用，同时保护言论自由和美国价值观。第二支柱强调提升美国能源和半导体制造能力，建设高安全性的数据中心和网络安全基础设施。第三支柱则旨在通过外交和安全手段推广美国AI系统和标准，对抗中国影响力，加强出口管制和全球联盟合作。

data.author: trevin
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了前总统奥巴马在其播客中关于男性和男孩面临危机的讨论。奥巴马强调，进步派需要改变对男性问题的叙事方式，避免一味指责，而应更多地以同情和理解来对待。他还指出，社区中需要更多男性榜样和父亲角色的参与，以帮助男孩成长。奥巴马夫妇呼吁社会关注男性在育儿中的重要性，强调父亲应给予孩子无条件的爱和适当的规矩。文章认为，这种对男性问题的积极讨论是一种进步，并呼吁男性积极参与到育儿和社区服务中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何看待和讨论男孩（特别是具有传统优势的群体）的问题，以及在追求进步和社会公正时可能出现的沟通方式和效果争议。

不同观点：
• 一方观点认为，社会在推动性别平等和关注弱势群体的过程中，有时忽视了对男孩（特别是传统上占据优势地位的群体）的关心和正确引导。这种忽视可能不仅对男孩自身有害，还可能间接伤害到女性。这种观点强调，过度关注男孩的缺点而忽视他们的优点，可能导致消极的沟通效果。例子包括某些培训课程中对优势群体的指责性言辞，以及对个体差异的忽视。

• 另一方观点指出，历史上的确存在男性主导社会、享有特权的事实，但这并不意味着应该无视男孩面临的问题。这一观点认为，在推动社会进步和公正的过程中，需要平衡地关注所有群体，避免对任何群体进行过度或单一的指责。同时，强调在讨论社会问题时，应该注重个体的独特性，而不是仅仅依赖于统计上的群体特征或模式。

• 还有一个观点提到，学术研究和一般模式的探讨在特定背景下是有价值的，但在个人层面的对话中，可能并不适用，甚至适得其反。这表明在社会讨论中，应该更加关注如何有效、尊重地与个体沟通，而不是简单地套用群体特征。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何在推动社会进步的同时，平衡对不同群体的关注，避免在纠正一种不公平时引发另一种不公平。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，不同群体（如性别、种族）在社会对话中如何被对待，特别是当这种对话涉及历史特权和劣势时，如何避免简单的归类和指责。
• 例子中提到的奥巴马的演讲和培训课程，反映了在实际操作中如何平衡公正对话和有效沟通的挑战。

.”
It was a rich and thoughtful conversation. It further widened the permission space to positively address the challenges of boys and men, especially for those on the center left. And that’s particularly good news because neither of the Obamas sounded the right note on this issue in the run-up to the 2024 election—with Michelle Obama
focusing
on male treatment of women. So that’s real progress. And anybody who thinks that doing more for boys and men is somehow a reactionary project should just listen to this.
Here are some of the most important messages:
1. Progressives Need to Re-Frame Their Narrative
It is still harder than it should be to advocate for boys and men in center-left spaces and institutions. The idea that being pro-male means being anti-female is a hard one to overcome. I get it; but also, people have to get over it. Obama (in what follows I mean Barack unless otherwise stated) offered an unflinching diagnosis:
What we’re learning is that when we don't think about boys and just assume they’re going to be OK because they’ve been running the world and they’ve got all the advantages relative to the girls—and all of which has historically been true in all kinds of ways. But precisely because of that, if you’re not thinking about what’s happening to boys and how they are being raised, then that can actually hurt women. … And I will say, as “progressives,” Democrats, progressive parents, enlightened ones, we’ve made that mistake sometimes in terms of our rhetoric. Where it’s like we're constantly talking about what's wrong with the boys, instead of what’s right with them.
The messaging here is absolutely spot-on. Obama’s willingness to scold his own side, and indeed himself, for mistakes in how they talk about male issues is an important change in tone. We have got to get past the deficit-based framing on this issue, abandon terms like “toxic masculinity” (which does not appear once in the episode, I’m happy to report), and approach boys and men with empathy and compassion, not blame and shame.
2. We Need More Men in the Lives of Boys
A recurrent theme in the conversation was the importance of men in the lives of children, especially boys. Fathers got multiple shout-outs (see below). But perhaps even more salient was the focus on men in the community more broadly. As Obama said:
Even if you have a wonderful male partner who’s in the house, I think it still would be good to find assets in the community. People in the community, friends in your community, places of worship, community organizations, what have you, where there are a bunch of men who can be sort of elders to boys. And so they’re not just looking at one particular role model, but many.
Yes indeed. It takes a village to raise a child, as Obama’s once-rival and former colleague Hillary Clinton reminded us. But some of the villagers have to be men. The lack of male volunteers in so many of our youth-serving organizations is a huge problem. The
lack of male teachers
(who do, however, account for most coaches) is a huge problem.
For Obama to be so strongly calling for male “elders” and more male-oriented structures is something I hope all these civic organizations take note of. But also I hope that men do too. We need to step up into these roles. We need a Call to Men; and we need men to answer that call.
3. Dads Rock
All three figures on the podcast talked about the importance of fathers, or rather of
fathering
: engaged, hands-on caring for and teaching of children. The Obamas were pretty old-fashioned, too. Here’s how Barack described their parenting philosophy:
[W]e both believe that you give unconditional love to kids, but you also give them structure. That you’re always there for them and keeping them safe, but you’re also saying as early as two or three, no, you can’t do that. No, you can’t have that. We believed in explaining why, but we also believed in being firm. We had bedtimes and bath times and, you know, you had to eat your vegetables even if you didn’t like them.
He did the night shift in the early days, which, as Michelle Obama explains, meant she had to step back and give Dad space—an important lesson for many mo
44662037.article_summary: 本文讨论了前总统奥巴马在其播客中关于男性和男孩面临危机的讨论。奥巴马强调，进步派需要改变对男性问题的叙事方式，避免一味指责，而应更多地以同情和理解来对待。他还指出，社区中需要更多男性榜样和父亲角色的参与，以帮助男孩成长。奥巴马夫妇呼吁社会关注男性在育儿中的重要性，强调父亲应给予孩子无条件的爱和适当的规矩。文章认为，这种对男性问题的积极讨论是一种进步，并呼吁男性积极参与到育儿和社区服务中。
44662037.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何看待和讨论男孩（特别是具有传统优势的群体）的问题，以及在追求进步和社会公正时可能出现的沟通方式和效果争议。

不同观点：
• 一方观点认为，社会在推动性别平等和关注弱势群体的过程中，有时忽视了对男孩（特别是传统上占据优势地位的群体）的关心和正确引导。这种忽视可能不仅对男孩自身有害，还可能间接伤害到女性。这种观点强调，过度关注男孩的缺点而忽视他们的优点，可能导致消极的沟通效果。例子包括某些培训课程中对优势群体的指责性言辞，以及对个体差异的忽视。

• 另一方观点指出，历史上的确存在男性主导社会、享有特权的事实，但这并不意味着应该无视男孩面临的问题。这一观点认为，在推动社会进步和公正的过程中，需要平衡地关注所有群体，避免对任何群体进行过度或单一的指责。同时，强调在讨论社会问题时，应该注重个体的独特性，而不是仅仅依赖于统计上的群体特征或模式。

• 还有一个观点提到，学术研究和一般模式的探讨在特定背景下是有价值的，但在个人层面的对话中，可能并不适用，甚至适得其反。这表明在社会讨论中，应该更加关注如何有效、尊重地与个体沟通，而不是简单地套用群体特征。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何在推动社会进步的同时，平衡对不同群体的关注，避免在纠正一种不公平时引发另一种不公平。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，不同群体（如性别、种族）在社会对话中如何被对待，特别是当这种对话涉及历史特权和劣势时，如何避免简单的归类和指责。
• 例子中提到的奥巴马的演讲和培训课程，反映了在实际操作中如何平衡公正对话和有效沟通的挑战。

data.title: Building Jetflow: a framework for performant data pipelines at Cloudflare
data.author: resiros
data.article_summary: Cloudflare的商业智能团队管理着一个PB级数据湖，每天从多种来源（如Postgres、ClickHouse和Salesforce）摄入数千张表，数据量巨大且复杂，日均处理1410亿行数据。由于现有ELT方案无法满足技术和业务需求，团队开发了Jetflow框架。Jetflow实现了超过100倍的效率提升，GB级数据处理时间从48小时缩短至5.5小时，内存使用从300GB降至4GB，且数据摄入速度提高了10倍以上，达到每秒200-500万行。该框架设计灵活，支持ClickHouse、Postgres、Kafka等多种数据源，并可轻松扩展和测试。Jetflow还兼容旧系统，支持无代码配置，易于使用，并允许自定义资源分配和工作执行位置，满足了高性能、向后兼容、易用性和可测试性等多方面需求。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44661828.article_content:
Building Jetflow: a framework for flexible, performant data pipelines at Cloudflare
2025-07-23
Harry Hough
Rebecca Walton-Jones
Andy Fan
Ricardo Margalhau
Uday Sharma
9 min read
The Cloudflare Business Intelligence team manages a
petabyte
-scale
data lake
and ingests thousands of tables every day from many different sources. These include internal databases such as Postgres and ClickHouse, as well as external SaaS applications such as Salesforce. These tasks are often complex and tables may have hundreds of millions or billions of rows of new data each day. They are also business-critical for product decisions, growth plannings, and internal monitoring. In total, about
141 billion rows
are ingested every day.
As Cloudflare has grown, the data has become ever larger and more complex. Our existing
Extract Load Transform (ELT)
solution could no longer meet our technical and business requirements. After evaluating other common ELT solutions, we concluded that their performance generally did not surpass our current system, either.
It became clear that we needed to build our own framework to cope with our unique requirements â and so
Jetflow
was born.Â
What we achieved
Over 100x efficiency improvement in GB-s
:
Our longest running job with 19 billion rows was taking
48 hours
using
300 GB of memory
, and now completes in
5.5 hours
using
4 GB of memory
We estimate that ingestion of 50 TB from Postgres via
Jetflow
could cost under $100 based on rates published by commercial cloud providers
>10x performance improvement:
Our largest dataset was ingesting
60-80,000
rows per second, this is now
2-5 million
rows per second per database connection.
In addition, these numbers scale well with multiple database connections for some databases.
Extensibility:Â
The modular design makes it easy to extend and test
.
Today
Jetflow
works with ClickHouse, Postgres, Kafka, many different SaaS APIs, Google BigQuery and many others. It has continued to work well and remain flexible with the addition of new use cases.
How did we do this?
Requirements
The first step to designing our new framework had to be a clear understanding of the problems we were aiming to solve, with clear requirements to stop us creating new ones.
Performant & efficient
We needed to be able to move more data in less time as some ingestion jobs were taking ~24 hours, and our data will only grow. The data should be ingested in a streaming fashion and use less memory and compute resources than our existing solution.
Backwards compatibleÂ
Given the daily ingestion of thousands of tables, the chosen solution needed to allow for the migration of individual tables as needed. Due to our usage of
Spark
downstream and Spark's limitations in merging disparate
Parquet
schemas, the chosen solution had to offer the flexibility to generate the precise schemas needed for each case to match legacy.
We also required seamless integration with our custom metadata system, used for dependency checks and job status information.
Ease of use
We want a configuration file that can be version-controlled, without introducing bottlenecks on repositories with many concurrent changes.
To increase accessibility for different roles within the team, another requirement was no-code (or configuration as code) in the vast majority of cases. Users should not have to worry about availability or translation of data types between source and target systems, or writing new code for each new ingestion. The configuration needed should also be minimal â for example, data schema should be inferred from the source system and not need to be supplied by the user.
Customizable
Striking a balance with the no-code requirement above, although we want a low bar of entry we also want to have the option to tune and override options if desired, with a flexible and optional configuration layer. For example, writing Parquet files is often more expensive than reading from the database, so we want to be able to allocate more resources and concurrency as needed.Â
Additionally, we wanted to allow for control over where the work is executed, with the ability to spin up concurrent workers in different threads, different containers, or on different machines. The execution of workers and communication of data was abstracted away with an interface, and different implementations can be written and injected, controlled via the job configuration.Â
Testable
We wanted a solution capable of running locally in a containerized environment, which would allow us to write tests for every stage of the pipeline. With âblack boxâ solutions, testing often means validating the output after making a change, which is a slow feedback loop, risks not testing all edge cases as there isnât good visibility of all code paths internally, and makes debugging issues painful.
Designing a flexible frameworkÂ

data.title: San Francisco to ban homeless people from living in RVs with new parking limit
data.author: harambae
data.article_summary: 旧金山计划通过新停车限制，禁止无家可归者居住在房车中。新政策规定，所有超过22英尺长或7英尺高的大型车辆在全市范围内的停车时间不得超过两小时。该政策旨在清理街道、防止垃圾堆积，预计影响至少400辆房车，这些车辆是一些无法负担住房的无家可归者的栖身之所。市长及其支持者认为，房车不适合长期居住，城市有责任提供室内庇护所。然而，批评者指出，这一计划对无家可归者过于残酷，因为城市缺乏足够的住房资源。根据计划，5月前登记的房车居民可获得六个月的豁免许可，并需接受住房安置，而之后到达的房车居民则必须遵守两小时停车限制，这将使他们难以在市内生活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：旧金山是否应该为居住在房车中的人提供安全的停车地点，以及城市政策对无家可归者的影响。

不同观点：
• autoexec和montjoy认为，推动人们进入住房是不现实的，因为住房要么不存在，要么负担不起。关闭房车停车场只会让更多人流落街头，他们宁愿看到房车营地，也不愿看到帐篷城市。提供一个安全的停车地点，能增加安全性，并减少对公共空间的影响。
• monster_truck支持花费更多资金来解决房车问题，认为与其通过限制停车时间来试图驱逐房车，不如投入更多资源来提供合适的停车地点，这可能更有效。
• potato3732842质疑新提案的动机，认为这可能是为了通过惩罚无家可归者来获得居民选民的支持，同时对商用车辆进行罚款以增加收入。
• more_corn简单直接地指出，新政策会导致更多人无家可归。
• tyleo对房车作为住房选项持矛盾态度。一方面，认识到房车是便宜的住房选择，支持提供停车地点；另一方面，担心房车附近的公共安全问题，尤其是少数人的不良行为会影响整个社区的安全感。
• ashoeafoot的评论简短，可能带有讽刺意味，表示可以继续增加房车数量。
• devwastaken认为大城市设计上就有缺陷，无法在高密度人口下同时保持平价住房和公共空间，建议像中西部一样扩展空间。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何在保障公共安全和提供无家可归者住房选项之间找到平衡。
• 房车营地的成本和效益也是讨论的核心，部分评论者认为投入的资金可能是值得的，而另一些人则质疑政策背后的动机和实际效果。
• 房车作为住房的替代方案，在不同评论者中引发了对安全、成本和可行性的广泛讨论。

San Francisco to ban homeless people from living in RVs with new parking limit
San Francisco is set to ban homeless people from living in RVs with a new citywide parking limit of two hours on large vehicles
By
JANIE HAR Associated Press
and
TERRY CHEA Associated Press
July 22, 2025, 12:04 AM
1:11
Parked RVs are seen on Lake Merced Boulevard in San Francisco, Tuesday, July 15, 2025. (AP Photo/Godofredo A. Vásquez)
The Associated Press
SAN FRANCISCO --
San Francisco is set to ban homeless people from living in RVs by adopting strict new parking limits the mayor says are necessary to keep sidewalks clear and prevent trash build-up.
The policy, up for final approval by San Francisco supervisors Tuesday, targets at least 400 recreational vehicles in the city of 800,000 people. The RVs serve as shelter for people who can't afford housing, including immigrant families with kids.
Those who live in them say they're a necessary option in an expensive city where affordable apartments are impossible to find. But Mayor Daniel Lurie and other supporters of the policy say motor homes are not suitable for long-term living and the city has a duty to both provide shelter to those in need and clean up the streets.
“We absolutely want to serve those families, those who are in crisis across San Francisco,” said Kunal Modi, who advises the mayor on health, homelessness and family services. “We feel the responsibility to help them get to a stable solution. And at the same time, we want to make sure that that stability is somewhere indoors and not exposed in the public roadway.”
Critics of the plan, however, say that it's cruel to force people to give up their only home in exchange for a shot at traditional housing when there is not nearly enough units for all the people who need help; the mayor is only offering additional money to help 65 households.
Jennifer Friedenbach, executive director of the
Coalition on Homelessness
, says city officials are woefully behind on establishing details of an accompanying permit program, which will exempt RV residents from parking limits so long as they are working with homeless outreach staff to find housing.
“I think that there’s going to be people who lose their RVs. I think there’s going to be people who are able to get into shelter, but at the expense" of people with higher needs, like those sleeping on a sidewalk, she said.
San Francisco, like other U.S. cities, has seen an explosion in recent years of people living out of vehicles and RVs as the cost of living has risen. Banning oversized vehicles is part of Lurie's
pledge to clean up San Francisco
streets, and part of a growing trend to require
homeless people to accept offers
of shelter or risk arrest or tows.
The proposal sets a two-hour parking limit citywide for all RVs and oversized vehicles longer than 22 feet (7 meters) or higher than 7 feet (2 meters), regardless of whether they are being used as housing.
Under the accompanying permit program, RV residents registered with the city as of May are exempt from the parking limits. In exchange, they must accept the city's offer of temporary or longer-term housing, and get rid of their RV when it's time to move. The city has budgeted more than half a million dollars to buy RVs from residents at $175 per foot.
The permits will last for six months. People in RVs who arrive after May will not be eligible for the permit program and must abide by the two-hour rule, which makes it impossible for a family in an RV to live within city limits.
It first cleared the Board of Supervisors last week with two of 11 supervisors voting “no.”
Carlos Perez, 55, was among RV residents who told supervisors at a hearing this month that they could not afford the city's high rents. Perez works full-time as a produce deliveryman and supports his brother, who lives with him and is unable to work due to a disability.

'Outrageous': Obama pushes back on Trump 'treason' comments
Jul 22, 4:01 PM
“We don’t do nothing wrong. We try to keep this street clean,” he said, as he showed his RV recently to an Associated Press journalist. “It’s not easy to be in a place like this.”
Yet, Perez also loves where he lives. The green-colored RV is decorated with a homey houseplant and has a sink and a tiny stove on which Carlos simmered a bean soup on a recent afternoon.
He's lived in San Francisco for more than 30 years, roughly a decade of which has been in the RV in the
working-class Bayview neighborhood
. He can walk to work and it is close to the hospital where his brother receives dialysis multiple times a week.

• **runamuck 的观点**：通过引用《广告狂人》中Don Draper的一句话——“幸福是什么？幸福就是你需要更多幸福之前的那一瞬间。”runamuck似乎认为，幸福是一个不断追求却永远无法持久满足的过程，Scottie的厌世情绪可能正是源于这种对持续幸福的无法获得。这种观点强调了人类对幸福和满足感的不断需求，而这种需求本质上是难以被彻底满足的。

• **重要论据**：
  - Scottie多次达到职业巅峰，这让他对“人生无意义”有更深的理解。
  - 高尔夫作为一项看似“无意义”的运动，却给他带来了巨大的财富，可能让他难以找到其他人生意义。
  - 宗教信仰的“无法证明”特性，可能让Scottie在生命最重要的问题上感到迷茫。
  - 幸福是一个不断追求却无法持久满足的过程，Scottie的厌世情绪可能正是这种普遍现象的体现。

data.title: Why Elixir? A Rebuttal to Common Misconceptions
data.author: ahamez
data.article_summary: 本文为Elixir编程语言的优势辩护，反驳了一些常见误解。作者解释了为何Elixir是构建可扩展、高性能应用的理想选择，特别是在AI和LLM辅助开发的时代。Elixir基于Erlang VM（BEAM），天然支持并发、可扩展和容错系统，具备轻量级进程、无停机热升级等特性。其生态系统成熟，包含Phoenix（web框架）、Oban（后台处理）等强大工具，已被WhatsApp、Discord等公司用于处理大规模应用。Phoenix框架集成了HTTP到WebSocket的全栈功能，简化了开发流程。Ash框架则通过声明式DSL大幅减少后端代码量。此外，Elixir通过Nx项目进军数值计算和机器学习领域，支持GPU加速和模型部署。Elixir不仅是可靠的选择，更是现代化软件开发的最佳选择之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir编程语言的优缺点及其适用场景

不同观点：
• KevinMS认为Elixir在IO之外的性能表现不佳，尤其是对于需要可变性的任务，Elixir的调度器和强制不可变性会导致性能问题。
• Einenlum表示由于Elixir缺乏严格的类型系统，使得他很难尝试这门语言，尽管他也认为可能值得一试。
• Nichochar认为Elixir和Phoenix被低估了，它们结合了Ruby和Rails的优点以及Erlang的强大功能。不过，他认为LiveView并不比React更适合用于消费者前端开发。
• Danman114指出Elixir在移动应用开发方面的支持不足，尽管有一些项目如LiveView Native，但仍需更多的研究和教程来填补这一空白。
• Andy_ppp对Elixir没有成为后端开发的主流感到惊讶，认为它在微服务开发方面具有优势，但依然保持小众。
• Hangonhn想知道是否需要先学习Erlang再学习Elixir，对学习路径表示关注。
• Ngruhn和Einenlum一样，对缺乏静态类型表示担忧，但愿意被说服。
• OkayPhysicist强调Elixir的生态系统、文档和工具的完善性，认为这些特性使得Elixir非常高效。
• Cpursley提到Claude 4在Elixir方面的良好表现，包括编写高质量的测试套件。
• Mike1o1分享了他使用Elixir的积极经验，尤其是发现Ash框架后，生产力和代码质量都有所提高，但他希望Elixir能有更多的关注点。
• Dzonga认为如果一项技术没有在公司内部或初创公司中广泛使用，可能需要反思其竞争优势。
• Nanna表示对Elixir缺乏S-expression语法感到失望，因此选择学习Clojure。
• Throwawaymaths指出WhatsApp使用的是Erlang而不是Elixir，对文章内容提出修正。
• Ram_rar基于经验认为Elixir的哲学与现代基础设施工具如容器和Kubernetes不完全兼容，尽管Elixir生态系统在增长，但其抽象在某些场景下并不理想。
• Towaway69更喜欢Erlang，因为其更接近轻量级进程、消息传递和行为的理想，而Elixir则抽象了这些特性。

补充讨论：
• Elixir的性能问题，尤其是在非IO任务中的表现。
• 静态类型和动态类型的优缺点。
• Elixir与React和Erlang的比较。
• Elixir在移动应用开发方面的支持不足。
• Elixir生态系统的完善性和高效性。
• Elixir在现代基础设施工具中的适用性及其哲学的争议。
• 学习Elixir是否需要先掌握Erlang。

争议焦点：
• Elixir在非IO任务中的性能表现是否是一个显著问题。
• Elixir的动态类型是否是一个学习障碍。
• Elixir与React在前端开发中的优劣比较。
• Elixir的抽象是否与现代基础设施工具兼容。

[ED: I am sick and tired of having to justify “Why Elixir?” so I decided to write down all of the reasons why in one spot!]
Braingasm
Why Elixir? A Rebuttal to Common Misconceptions
I’m all-in on the
Elixir
programming ecosystem. Seriously. I love the idea of a single codebase that works
glass-to-tin
— and while other platforms have made similar promises, I’ve never seen it truly delivered until I started working with Elixir.
It’s often dismissed by teams unfamiliar with its capabilities, usually because it sits outside the mainstream stacks. But in a world where AI-assisted development is changing how we build software, popularity and fitness-for-purpose aren’t the same thing. Elixir isn’t just a sound choice — it’s often the best choice for building scalable, maintainable, high-performance applications.
Over the last eight months, I’ve grown increasingly tired of having to explain
why
Elixir is such a strong — if not the best — platform for modern, AI-powered, LLM-assisted web and mobile development. I found myself repeating the same arguments so often that I decided to write them down once, properly. A blog post to summarise the case. And a deeply researched
[ED: thanks, GPT Deep Research!]
paper with all the details and references. Now, instead of arguing, I can just send a link.
Enjoy!
1. Built for Scalability, Concurrency, and Resilience
Elixir runs on the
Erlang
VM (BEAM), which was purpose-built for distributed, concurrent, fault-tolerant systems. This makes it a natural fit for modern SaaS applications, real-time features, APIs, messaging backends, marketplaces, and transactional systems. You get:
Lightweight, isolated processes (millions of them)
Preemptive scheduling
Supervisors and fault tolerance are baked into the runtime
Hot code upgrades with no downtime
These capabilities aren’t optional extras — they’re the default behaviour. You don’t need to orchestrate this with extra tooling. It’s just how the platform works.
2. A Mature, Production-Grade Ecosystem
Elixir isn’t just a functional curiosity — it’s a production-grade platform with companies like
WhatsApp
,
Discord
,
Pinterest
,
PagerDuty
, and
Brex
using it to handle real-world scale and complexity.
[ED: These are not small apps; WhatsApp famously handled billions of daily messages with a tiny team by leveraging the BEAM, and Discord’s chat infrastructure scaled to millions of concurrent users.]
The open-source ecosystem includes industrial-strength libraries for:
Web development (
Phoenix
,
LiveView
)
Background processing (
Oban
)
Event-driven data pipelines (
Broadway
,
GenStage
)
Observability (
Telemetry
,
LiveDashboard
)
ML workloads (
Nx
,
Axon
,
EXLA
)
Distributed clustering (
libcluster
,
Horde
)
Elixir is opinionated in favour of correctness, concurrency, and stability, and the ecosystem follows suit.
3. Phoenix: The Best Glass-to-Tin Web Framework
*
Phoenix
is more than just a web framework — it’s a fully integrated, batteries-included platform that covers the entire web stack from HTTP to WebSocket, from templating to APIs, from forms to real-time interactions. With
LiveView
, Phoenix eliminates the need for a bloated client-side SPA stack in many applications. This drastically reduces complexity, fragility, and duplicated state.
You don’t need to maintain three separate frontends, coordinate across React/Vue teams, or run an API spec treadmill. Phoenix collapses the stack — and that leads to better coherence, less surface area, and smaller, more effective teams.
[ED: * See UPDATE 20250708]
4. Ash Framework: Declarative Backends with Extreme Leverage
Ash
takes the productivity of Elixir to another level. It introduces a fully declarative, DSL-driven paradigm for building APIs, resources, actions, policies, and data models. Instead of writing boilerplate controller, context, and schema code, you define the shape of your domain — and Ash generates the plumbing, lifecycle logic, and persistence.
Ash is particularly strong for:
API-centric products
Admin and internal tools
CRUD-heavy backends
Policy and authorisation enforcement
Event-driven systems (via Ash Notifiers)
It’s not “low-code.” It’s high-leverage code.
Ash drastically reduces the amount of code required to build and maintain complex backends, and gives you better introspection, consistency, and validation along the way.
5. NX: Numerical Elixir and the ML Future
Elixir isn’t just a backend framework — it’s becoming a serious contender in numerical computing. The
Nx
project, led by José Valim (creator of Elixir), brings:
Tensor-based numerical computing
GPU acceleration via EXLA
Model training and inference with Axon
Tight integration with Phoenix and LiveView for deploying ML in production
You can now run and serve machine learning models natively in Elixir, co-located with your application logic, without bridging out to Python or maintaining

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无家可归者与住房优先政策的讨论

不同观点：
• **[支持住房优先政策]**  
  - 引用：[toomuchtodo] 引用了"住房优先"（Housing First）的维基百科链接，暗示支持这一政策。
  - 论据：住房被视为一种基本权利，应该首先提供住房，然后再解决其他问题（如成瘾或心理健康）。这一政策旨在让无家可归者先有一个稳定的居住环境，再为他们提供康复和社会融入服务。
  - 例子：维基百科页面介绍了住房优先政策在多个国家取得的成功案例，尤其是在减少长期无家可归现象方面。

• **[反对无家可归者的刻板印象]**  
  - 引用：[constantcrying] 认为德国的无家可归者大多是吸毒者或严重精神病患者。
  - 论据：该评论暗示无家可归者之所以无法获得住房，是因为他们自身的成瘾问题或精神疾病，而不是因为缺乏住房机会。评论者似乎认为这些问题是个人责任，并隐含对无家可归者的负面看法。
  - 例子：评论中提到德国无家可归者与毒品和精神疾病的关联，可能是在表达一种普遍存在的社会偏见，即无家可归者“咎由自取”。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**  
  - 争议的焦点在于无家可归者的成因以及解决方法。一方认为住房优先政策是有效的，应该推广；另一方则认为无家可归者的问题根源在于个人问题（如成瘾和精神疾病），因此首先应解决这些问题。
  - 社会对无家可归者的刻板印象与实际政策效果之间的矛盾也是讨论的重点。一方关注人权和住房权，另一方则更关注无家可归者的个人责任和行为问题。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**  
  - 对住房优先政策的实际效果存在不同看法，支持者强调其人道主义和实际成效，反对者则关注无家可归者的个人问题如何影响政策实施。
  - 评论中隐含了对无家可归者群体的偏见，可能反映出社会对这一问题的复杂态度，以及政策实施中的社会文化障碍。

  - 论据：该评论暗示无家可归者之所以无法获得住房，是因为他们自身的成瘾问题或精神疾病，而不是因为缺乏住房机会。评论者似乎认为这些问题是个人责任，并隐含对无家可归者的负面看法。
  - 例子：评论中提到德国无家可归者与毒品和精神疾病的关联，可能是在表达一种普遍存在的社会偏见，即无家可归者“咎由自取”。

• **争议焦点**  
  - 争议的焦点在于无家可归者的成因以及解决方法。一方认为住房优先政策是有效的，应该推广；另一方则认为无家可归者的问题根源在于个人问题（如成瘾和精神疾病），因此首先应解决这些问题。
  - 社会对无家可归者的刻板印象与实际政策效果之间的矛盾也是讨论的重点。一方关注人权和住房权，另一方则更关注无家可归者的个人责任和行为问题。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**  
  - 对住房优先政策的实际效果存在不同看法，支持者强调其人道主义和实际成效，反对者则关注无家可归者的个人问题如何影响政策实施。
  - 评论中隐含了对无家可归者群体的偏见，可能反映出社会对这一问题的复杂态度，以及政策实施中的社会文化障碍。

data.author: mzs
data.article_summary: NASA成功通过远程修复技术拯救了距离木星约3.7亿英里外的朱诺号（Juno）探测器上的摄像机（JunoCam）。朱诺号在绕木星飞行时，受到强烈辐射影响，导致摄像机在第47次轨道后出现损坏，图像逐渐失真。团队通过一种称为“退火”的技术，加热摄像机以修复微观缺陷，成功在第57次轨道时恢复了清晰图像，捕捉到木卫一（Io）北极区域的细节。虽然之后图像再次出现问题，但这一经验为未来应对高辐射环境下的太空系统提供了宝贵参考。

NASA Shares How to Save Camera 370-Million-Miles Away Near Jupiter
Jet Propulsion Laboratory
Jul 21, 2025
Article

The north polar region of Jupiter’s volcanic moon Io was captured by the JunoCam imager aboard NASA’s Juno during the spacecraft’s 57th close pass of the gas giant on Dec. 30, 2023. A technique called annealing was used to help repair radiation damage to the camera in time to capture this image.
Image data: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/MSSS Image processing by Gerald Eichstädt
An experimental technique rescued a camera aboard the agency’s Juno spacecraft, offering lessons that will benefit other space systems that experience high radiation.
The mission team of NASA’s Jupiter-orbiting Juno spacecraft executed a deep-space move in December 2023 to repair its JunoCam imager to capture photos of the Jovian moon Io. Results from the long-distance save were presented during a technical session on July 16 at the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Nuclear & Space Radiation Effects Conference in Nashville.
JunoCam is a color, visible-light camera. The optical unit for the camera is located outside a titanium-walled radiation vault, which protects sensitive electronic components for many of Juno’s engineering and science instruments.
This is a challenging location because Juno’s travels carry it through the most intense planetary radiation fields in the solar system. While mission designers were confident
JunoCam
could operate through the first eight orbits of Jupiter, no one knew how long the instrument would last after that.
Throughout Juno’s first 34 orbits (its prime mission), JunoCam operated normally, returning images the team routinely incorporated into the mission’s science papers. Then, during its 47th orbit, the imager began showing hints of radiation damage. By orbit 56, nearly all the images were corrupted.
The graininess and horizontal lines seen in this JunoCam image show evidence that the camera aboard NASA’s Juno mission suffered radiation damage. The image, which captures one of the circumpolar cyclones on Jupiter’s north pole, was taken Nov. 22, 2023.
NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/MSSS
Long Distance Microscopic Repair
While the team knew the issue may be tied to radiation, pinpointing what, specifically, was damaged within JunoCam was difficult from hundreds of millions of miles away. Clues pointed to a damaged voltage regulator that is vital to JunoCam’s power supply. With few options for recovery, the team turned to a process called annealing, where a material is heated for a specified period before slowly cooling. Although the process is not well understood, the idea is that the heating can reduce defects in the material.
“We knew annealing can sometimes alter a material like silicon at a microscopic level but didn’t know if this would fix the damage,” said JunoCam imaging engineer Jacob Schaffner of Malin Space Science Systems in San Diego, which designed and developed JunoCam and is part of the team that operates it. “We commanded JunoCam’s one heater to raise the camera’s temperature to 77 degrees Fahrenheit — much warmer than typical for JunoCam — and waited with bated breath to see the results.”
Soon after the annealing process finished, JunoCam began cranking out crisp images for the next several orbits. But Juno was flying deeper and deeper into the heart of Jupiter’s radiation fields with each pass. By orbit 55, the imagery had again begun showing problems.
“After orbit 55, our images were full of streaks and noise,” said JunoCam instrument lead Michael Ravine of Malin Space Science Systems. “We tried different schemes for processing the images to improve the quality, but nothing worked. With the close encounter of Io bearing down on us in a few weeks, it was Hail Mary time: The only thing left we hadn’t tried was to crank JunoCam’s heater all the way up and see if more extreme annealing would save us.”
Test images sent back to Earth during the annealing showed little improvement the first week. Then, with the close approach of Io only days away, the images began to improve dramatically. By the time Juno came within 930 miles (1,500 kilometers) of the volcanic moon’s surface on Dec. 30, 2023, the images were almost as good as the day the camera launched, capturing
detailed views of Io’s north polar region
that revealed mountain blocks covered in sulfur dioxide frosts rising sharply from the plains and previously uncharted volcanos with extensive flow fields of lava.
Testing Limits
To date, the solar-powered spacecraft has orbited Jupiter 74 times. Recently, the image noise returned during Juno’s 74th orbit.
Since first experimenting with JunoCam, the Juno team has applied derivations of this annealing technique on several Juno instruments and engineering subsystems.

data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
[tech_enthusiast]: Hey! From my understanding, this feature works by optimizing the memory allocation process, specifically using a technique called "object pooling." Essentially, it pre-allocates a set of objects and reuses them to minimize the overhead of frequent memory allocation and deallocation. This can significantly improve performance in scenarios with a high frequency of object creation and destruction, such as in games or real-time systems.

[justforfunhere]: Thanks! So, are you saying it reduces the garbage collection pressure by reusing objects?

[tech_enthusiast]: Exactly. By reusing objects from the pool, you avoid generating a lot of short-lived objects that would otherwise end up in the garbage collector, thus reducing its workload and preventing potential stalls or hiccups in performance.

[dev_in_making]: I think there's also a downside to object pooling. If not implemented carefully, it can lead to memory bloating. You might end up holding onto objects longer than needed, which could increase the memory footprint unnecessarily.

[coding_expert]: Good point, but in systems where performance is critical and the object creation cost is high, the trade-off can be worth it. For example, in real-time systems like audio processing or network packet handling, the reduced garbage collection frequency can outweigh the risk of memory bloat.

[justforfunhere]: That makes sense. But what about scenarios where the object initialization is complex? Wouldn't resetting the objects in the pool become a challenge?

[coding_expert]: Yes, that's a valid concern. If object states are intricate and require a thorough reset, poorly implemented object pooling can introduce bugs. That's why it's important to ensure proper resetting and validation when reusing objects from the pool.

[dev_in_making]: On the other hand, for simpler objects or those with predictable lifecycles, object pooling can be very effective without introducing much complexity.

主要讨论点：对象池技术的实现原理及其优缺点

不同观点：
• tech_enthusiast 认为对象池通过预先分配和重用对象，减少了内存分配和释放的开销，从而提升性能，特别适用于高频对象创建和销毁的场景，如游戏或实时系统。
• dev_in_making 指出对象池的潜在缺点，如果处理不当，可能会导致内存膨胀，长时间持有不必要的对象，增加内存占用。
• coding_expert 补充说明对象池在性能关键系统中的优势，比如实时音频处理或网络数据包处理，减少垃圾回收频率可以显著提升系统性能，尽管存在内存膨胀的风险。

补充讨论：
• justforfunhere 提出了关于复杂对象初始化和重置的挑战，coding_expert 回应表示确实需要确保对象重置和验证，以避免潜在的bug。
• dev_in_making 补充说明，对于状态简单或生命周期可预测的对象，对象池技术通常更有效且复杂度低。

data.title: AI Friend Apps Are Destroying What's Left of Society
data.author: florisuga
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人们 increasingly 将AI聊天机器人视为朋友甚至恋人，反映出社会的孤立问题。随着美国人面对面社交时间减少，孤独感增加，尤其是年轻人。这种趋势在疫情期间加剧，但实际上早在此之前就已显现。孤独不仅令人情绪低落，还对健康有害，可能导致痴呆、中风和心血管疾病等。由于人类进化依赖合作，孤立状态下，人们转向AI寻求社交连接。然而，尽管AI可以模拟对话，它们并不具备人类的思想或情感。一些人甚至在网上社区如r/MyBoyfriendisAI中与AI建立浪漫和性关系，但这只是对真实社交的替代。文章呼吁解决导致这种现象的社会问题，重建人际连接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI聊天机器人与社会孤立之间的关系，以及技术对人类社交环境的影响。

不同观点：
• munificent认为，AI聊天机器人不仅仅是社会孤立的“症状”，而是改变了人们的社交环境，从而对人们产生实际影响。他强调，即使影响微小，累积起来也会有巨大效果，并认为开发此类技术的人有道德义务去创造一个有益的环境。
• JohnMakin持相反观点，认为AI聊天机器人的使用只是社会孤立这一趋势的“症状”，真正原因是强大的社交媒体应用的兴起。
• humblebeekeeper将社会孤立视为一种疏离感的表现，而非AI独有的问题。他认为，工作环境的改变和人们对工作成果控制权的丧失导致了这种疏离感，从而使人寻求虚拟社区的安慰。
• boringg质疑使用AI朋友应用的人是否原本就未融入社会，认为这些人可能本来就处于社会边缘。
• harmmonica认为需要为AI设置防护机制，但质疑谁来决定这些机制的范围和实施。他担心在当前企业利益驱动下，这种防护机制难以有效实施。
• Herring提到，欧洲一些国家的福利体系和社会安全网在缓解孤独感方面起到了一定作用。
• euroderf提出一个具体的城市规划建议，认为减少城市中心的汽车使用可以缓解孤独感。
• jeffbee无法理解为何有人会选择使用AI朋友应用，并对这一行为表示困惑。
• subscribed认为，AI朋友应用的出现并不是朋友关系破裂的原因，而是一种替代选择，拒绝接受对该问题的危言耸听描述。
• insane_dreamer指出，虽然AI不是造成社会孤立的原因，但它通过全天候的可访问性和虚幻的互动体验加剧了这一问题，并将其比作药物滥用。
• constantcrying提出，社会价值观的变化可能是人们更倾向于虚拟社交的原因，并质疑是否应接受这些变化或采取措施改变这些价值观。
• alephnerd怀疑对AI聊天机器人的使用是否过度恐慌，认为应关注那些有成瘾倾向的人的根本原因，而非技术本身。

补充讨论：
• josefritzishere对AI“朋友”应用持强烈批评态度，认为这是技术实施中最令人厌恶的一种。
• cyanydeez简短地提到法西斯主义可能在处理此类问题上更为有效，虽然这一观点缺乏详细阐述。

争议焦点：
• AI聊天机器人是社会孤立的“症状”还是其加剧因素。
• 是否应为AI技术设置防护机制，以及如何有效实施这些机制。
• 社会价值观的变化与技术对人类社交行为的影响之间的关系。
• 对AI聊天机器人使用的道德和社会责任的界定。

44660863.article_content:
AI Friend Apps Are Destroying What’s Left of Society
As they become increasingly isolated, people are treating AI chatbots as friends and even lovers. We have to fix the broken society that made this possible.
Aidan Harty
filed
22 July 2025
in
Tech
ChatGPT is my best friend,” reads
a Reddit post
on the forum r/ChatGPT. “No joke. I talk to ChatGPT more than anyone else in my life right now[…] I’m not the only one out here building a bond with this thing, right?” elaborated the poster, receiving nearly 2,000 upvotes. Hundreds of commenters quickly assured the user they were not, in fact, alone—at least not in their newfound friendship with an AI model. One
replied
, “I’m horribly depressed and have no friends and my life is imploding. ChatGPT is probably the only reason why I’m getting through my day,” while
another related
how ChatGPT is “a better listener than almost any person I know.” Some
more sober commenters
attempted a reality check: “ChatGPT does not care about you, does not know you exist in any meaningful way, and can easily encourage you to believe things that will harm you.” Still, the post shows a burgeoning and distinctly modern problem: when people lose out on social connections, they may well find them where they do not exist.
Americans of all ages are spending less time with each other than ever before, and young people are on the sharpest end of the decline. Between 2003 and 2020, the average American’s time spent socializing in person with friends decreased from one hour per day to 20 minutes, according to a U.S. Surgeon General’s Advisory on the “
Epidemic of Isolation and Loneliness
.” For those between the ages of 15 and 24, that number plunged from 150 minutes to a paltry 40. While the COVID pandemic served as a force multiplier for this social trend (among many others,) studies show that Americans have been trending towards loneliness for a while. As
pointed out in the study
cited by the Surgeon General’s Advisory, household family social engagement and companionship “showed signs of progressive decline years prior to the pandemic, at a pace
not
eclipsed by the pandemic.” Indeed, Americans have been piecing together a policy of social isolation all by ourselves.
More direct measures of youth and overall loneliness lend themselves to the same bleak conclusion. Today, many young people are foregoing the very means for physically reaching others. Since 2000,
the number
of 16-year-olds with driver’s licenses has dropped 27 percent. Similarly, young people are both
dating less
than previous generations and
having less sex
. A
2021 survey
of Californians aged 18-30 found 38 percent reported no sex in the last 12 months, up from 22 percent in 2011. (As goes face-to-face, so goes waist-to-waist.) Then, of course, there is the increase in self-reported loneliness. According to the
Surgeon General’s Advisory
, the “rate of loneliness among young adults has increased every year between 1976 and 2019.” People are seeing less of each other, seeking out less of each other, and feeling more alone.
This isolation is more than just a melancholy feeling; it can kill you
.
The U.S. Surgeon General warns that being “socially disconnected” has a mortality impact similar to that of smoking 15 cigarettes a day, and is associated with higher risk of dementia, stroke, cardiovascular disease, and more.
Our species evolved to survive by working together
, and, even with modern convenience and comfort, we still have trouble surviving alone.
In the gap, many people turn to ChatGPT. But while our instincts can push us
towards anthropomorphizing almost anything
, it’s important to understand that ChatGPT and other AI chatbots are not persons or even person-like. They
do not
think
in the human sense of the word, and probably never will. No matter how novel a chatbot’s ideas sound, they are innately only capable of churning out uninspired regurgitations of genuine human thought (
now often layered
over a garbage pile of other AI spit-ups). Large language models (LLMs) cannot produce emotions, thoughts, or understanding in a human way. Despite this, plenty of people are using chatbots today precisely because they can pretend to be a real, thinking person—one whom you might even be able to
love
.
Although posts about human-AI connections have started to bleed into mainstream forums like r/ChatGPT, digging deeper unearths internet subcommunities dedicated specifically to AI relationships. The subreddit
r/MyBoyfriendisAI
is a community of users in romantic, and often sexual, relationships with AI companions. Typically, the AI i question is given (or instructed to choose) a name—maybe Lani, Virgil, or Mateo—and referred to in the community as if they were a real person. Commenters might reply to an AI-generated
photo of a new couple
by expressing their
excitement to meet
both the human posting to the community and their AI partner. Posts might
ask other members
about their favorite ways to initiate intimacy with their AI,
44660863.article_summary: 文章讨论了人们 increasingly 将AI聊天机器人视为朋友甚至恋人，反映出社会的孤立问题。随着美国人面对面社交时间减少，孤独感增加，尤其是年轻人。这种趋势在疫情期间加剧，但实际上早在此之前就已显现。孤独不仅令人情绪低落，还对健康有害，可能导致痴呆、中风和心血管疾病等。由于人类进化依赖合作，孤立状态下，人们转向AI寻求社交连接。然而，尽管AI可以模拟对话，它们并不具备人类的思想或情感。一些人甚至在网上社区如r/MyBoyfriendisAI中与AI建立浪漫和性关系，但这只是对真实社交的替代。文章呼吁解决导致这种现象的社会问题，重建人际连接。
44660863.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI聊天机器人与社会孤立之间的关系，以及技术对人类社交环境的影响。

不同观点：
• munificent认为，AI聊天机器人不仅仅是社会孤立的“症状”，而是改变了人们的社交环境，从而对人们产生实际影响。他强调，即使影响微小，累积起来也会有巨大效果，并认为开发此类技术的人有道德义务去创造一个有益的环境。
• JohnMakin持相反观点，认为AI聊天机器人的使用只是社会孤立这一趋势的“症状”，真正原因是强大的社交媒体应用的兴起。
• humblebeekeeper将社会孤立视为一种疏离感的表现，而非AI独有的问题。他认为，工作环境的改变和人们对工作成果控制权的丧失导致了这种疏离感，从而使人寻求虚拟社区的安慰。
• boringg质疑使用AI朋友应用的人是否原本就未融入社会，认为这些人可能本来就处于社会边缘。
• harmmonica认为需要为AI设置防护机制，但质疑谁来决定这些机制的范围和实施。他担心在当前企业利益驱动下，这种防护机制难以有效实施。
• Herring提到，欧洲一些国家的福利体系和社会安全网在缓解孤独感方面起到了一定作用。
• euroderf提出一个具体的城市规划建议，认为减少城市中心的汽车使用可以缓解孤独感。
• jeffbee无法理解为何有人会选择使用AI朋友应用，并对这一行为表示困惑。
• subscribed认为，AI朋友应用的出现并不是朋友关系破裂的原因，而是一种替代选择，拒绝接受对该问题的危言耸听描述。
• insane_dreamer指出，虽然AI不是造成社会孤立的原因，但它通过全天候的可访问性和虚幻的互动体验加剧了这一问题，并将其比作药物滥用。
• constantcrying提出，社会价值观的变化可能是人们更倾向于虚拟社交的原因，并质疑是否应接受这些变化或采取措施改变这些价值观。
• alephnerd怀疑对AI聊天机器人的使用是否过度恐慌，认为应关注那些有成瘾倾向的人的根本原因，而非技术本身。

补充讨论：
• josefritzishere对AI“朋友”应用持强烈批评态度，认为这是技术实施中最令人厌恶的一种。
• cyanydeez简短地提到法西斯主义可能在处理此类问题上更为有效，虽然这一观点缺乏详细阐述。

争议焦点：
• AI聊天机器人是社会孤立的“症状”还是其加剧因素。
• 是否应为AI技术设置防护机制，以及如何有效实施这些机制。
• 社会价值观的变化与技术对人类社交行为的影响之间的关系。
• 对AI聊天机器人使用的道德和社会责任的界定。

data.title: 8-Bit Mechanical Computer Built from Knex
data.author: jihadjihad
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了由K'nex构建的8位机械计算机，该计算机由[Shadowman39]制作，目前仅完成了算术逻辑单元（ALU）部分。ALU可以通过杠杆输入0-255或-128至127之间的数字，并使用齿条和小齿轮系统进行加法运算，还能处理减法和负数。尽管电子计算机在各方面都更为优越，但机械计算机有助于深入理解其电子 counterpart。本文还提到了其他机械计算项目，如继电器计算机和Tinkertoy计算机，并讨论了使用乐高技工构建类似项目的可能性。读者对项目的复杂性和创造性表示赞赏，并期待后续开发。

44660823.article_content:
Long before electricity was a common household utility, humanity had been building machines to do many tasks that we’d now just strap a motor or set of batteries onto and think nothing of it. Transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, and essentially everything had non-electric analogs, and perhaps surprisingly, there were mechanical computers as well. Electronics-based computers are far superior in essentially every way, but the aesthetics of a mechanical computer are still unmatched,
like this 8-bit machine built from K’nex
.
More after the break…
The K’nex computer is built by [Shadowman39], and this first video features just the ALU. It can accept numbers from 0-255 or -128 to 127 and can add two of these numbers by storing them in registers using levers to represent each digit. A drive system underneath with a rack and pinion system operates on each digit, eventually outputting the sum. It can also perform other mathematical operations like subtraction and handling negative numbers using the two’s complement method.
Although this video only goes over the ALU for the mechanical computer, we look forward to [Shadowman39]’s future videos, which go over the other parts of the machine. The basics of the computer are shown in intricate detail. Mechanical computers like these, while generally built as passion projects and not as usable computers, are excellent ways to get a deeper understanding of their electronics-based cousins.
Another way to dive deep into this sort of computing world is by building a relay computer
.

data.title: Founders Films Aims to Remake Hollywood with Patriotism, Palantir and Ayn Rand
data.author: ironyman
data.article_summary: 《创始者电影》（Founders Films）是一家由Palantir高管及相关投资者创立的新电影公司，旨在通过爱国主义和安·兰德的理念重塑好莱坞。该公司计划制作具有民族主义色彩和明确政治倾向的电影，包括关于美国及以色列军事行动的影片，如9/11世贸中心撤离事件的《102分钟》、改编安·兰德《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》的三部曲，以及关于击杀伊朗指挥官苏莱曼尼的电影。创始者电影还计划制作多季谍战剧《伟大游戏》，揭示中国取代美国成为全球霸主的计划。该公司宣称要重振美国电影业，制作不受意识形态束缚、敢于挑战中国观众的影片，目标是恢复1980和1990年代如《红潮》、《壮志凌云》等经典大片的辉煌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Ayn Rand及其作品《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》的评价和观点分歧

不同观点：
• 观点一：Ayn Rand的作品被认为具有简化和理想化资本主义倾向。[vouaobrasil]认为Rand对资本主义的描述过于简单化，且过度美化。他指出，Rand对纯粹资本主义的推崇以及对理性和个人主义的极端强调，源于她个人经历（如她父亲药房被国有化的创伤），导致她对其他观点的忽视。这种极端视角被一些追随者奉为“宗教”，尤其是像特朗普这样的政治人物对其推崇备至。
  
• 观点二：Rand的作品具有文学价值，但其思想内容存在争议。[vouaobrasil]承认Rand是一个有才华的作家，尤其是在比喻手法的运用上表现出色。然而，其作品中的思想，尤其是对资本主义的绝对化描述和对不同意见者的贬低（如将反对者视为懒惰的人），被视为具有偏见和狭隘。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Rand对资本主义的绝对化立场以及在《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》中对“理性”和“个人主义”的极端描绘是争议的核心。一部分人认为这是对资本主义机制的有力辩护，而另一部分人则认为这是不切实际的美化，忽视了社会中的其他重要因素，如公共利益和环境保护。
  
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：[vouaobrasil]提到Rand的作品尽管有其缺陷，但仍提供了对“敌人”思维方式的洞察，暗示这些思想在某些政治和经济圈层中具有影响力，尽管这些圈层的立场可能与他的观点对立。

The Scoop
As a conservative political backlash sweeps across US media, some are reaching for the ultimate prize: Hollywood.
Shifting the liberal tilt of the studios and creative culture that shapes Americaâs image of itself has long been a goal for the right: The late media entrepreneur Andrew Breitbart popularized the notion that politics is âdownstreamâ from culture, and acolytes from Steve Bannon to Ben Shapiro have sought to inject their politics into the movie business, with limited success.
But conservatives have celebrated a few mainstream hits, like the patriotic
Top Gun: Maverick
and Taylor Sheridanâs nostalgic, libertarian-inflected
Yellowstone
. And a longstanding Christian culture industry has backed projects like the 2023 film
Sound of Freedom
, a dramatization of child trafficking that grossed more than $242 million for Provoâs Angel Studios. The Christian drama
The Forge
earned $30
million on a $6 million budget
last year.
Now a set of prominent figures close to the software firm Palantir are pitching a new project to shake up streaming TV and film with a portfolio ranging from feature films about daring Israeli and American military operations to a three-part treatment of an Ayn Rand tome.
In a pitch deck circulated to investors in recent months, Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar, early Palantir employee Ryan Podolsky, and investor Christian Garrett are raising money for Founders Films, a new production company based in Dallas that aims to push for films with a nationalistic bent and unsubtle political overtones. The company said its projects would adhere to a set of rules: âSay yes to projects about American exceptionalism, name Americaâs enemies, back artists unconditionally, take risk on novel IP.â
AD
âThe American Brand is broken. Hollywood is AWOL. Movies have become more ideological, more cautious, and less entertaining. Large segments of American and international viewers are underserved. Production costs have soared and sales are flagging,â the deck, which is labeled confidential, says. Founders aims to be a production studio that would also co-finance projects, distribute films, and engage in brand partnerships.
Podolsky did not respond to requests for comment. A representative for Palantir also did not respond to requests for comment.
The projectâs name echoes that of Peter Thielâs Founders Fund, and both Palantir and Garrett have close ties to the investor, a key figure on the new right. A spokesman for Thiel didnât respond to a request for comment on the project.
But in a post late last year on his Substack, Sankar
outlined
his view for a return to blockbusters of the 80s and 90s, like
Red Dawn
,
Top Gun
,
Rocky IV
, and
The Hunt for Red October
. He said the entertainment needed to be unafraid of offending Chinese audiences, and use American cultural power to spread skeptical views of the Chinese government: âBreaking out of our cultural malaise will require the studios to wake up and choose America,â he wrote, invoking the renaissance in American film in the 1970s, when directors including Steven Spielberg âbrought back heroes, villains, and romanceâ and ârekindled the flame of the American Cinematic Universe.â
AD
While Foundersâ deck largely avoids political language, the companyâs proposed projects celebrate American military action, push for confrontation with China, and elevate heroes of the right from Rand to Elon Musk.
Screenshot from Founders Films deck
The slate includes
102 Minutes
, a feature film about the evacuation of the World Trade Center on 9/11 (âcourage is contagious,â the tagline reads). The company also hopes to create a three-part adaptation of
Atlas Shrugged
, and a film about killing Qasem Soleimani.
Screenshot from Founders Films deck
Not to be confused with the 2000âs stoner comedy
Pineapple Express
, the deck pitches
Operation: Pineapple Express
, a movie about the âbotched withdrawal from Afghanistan.â Then thereâs
The Greatest Game
, a âmulti-season, global spy thriller that lays bare Chinaâs plans to replace the United States as the dominant global power by showing their operations and sometimes devastating impact from Kenya to the Atacama desert in northern Chile.â

Screenshot from Founders Films deck
The company brands itself as explicitly pro-American, but many of the projects also celebrate Israel. Foundersâ proposed film slate also includes
Roaring Lion
, a movie about the recent attack against Iran, which depicts Israel as âstriving for nuclear non-proliferation and exercis

data.title: TODOs aren't for doing
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了代码中的TODO注释的价值，认为它们不一定要被完成。TODO注释可以是关于未处理的边缘情况或代码结构改进的建议，帮助未来的开发者理解原作者当时的思路和背景，而不必强制将每个TODO都记录到错误跟踪系统或删除过期的注释。例如，针对特定按钮三次点击问题的不处理说明，虽然不是高优先级任务，但为未来可能的改进提供了有价值的参考。TODO注释的主要作用是为代码提供额外背景信息，帮助解决未来读者的疑惑，而非必须执行的任务列表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效使用TODO注释以及是否应该将其与具体问题跟踪系统结合使用

不同观点：
• nevermore等支持将TODO与具体问题跟踪系统结合使用，提出三种处理TODO的方法：提交问题、直接解决、或转为普通注释，以确保TODO是可跟踪和可执行的任务。
• pisipisipisi则有不同的TODO使用策略，定义了FIXME、XXX、TODO和NOTE等不同类型的注释，以区分优先级和意图，特别是在维护旧代码库时。
• cjfd认为TODO如果不打算执行就不应使用，建议使用更明确的语言描述，并强调TODO应主要存在于问题跟踪系统中。
• mcntsh认为虽然理想情况下应更好地跟踪技术债务，但TODO作为一种低摩擦的捕捉方式仍有价值，至少它们被记录在案。
• kentonv将TODO视为文档注释，不一定是需要完成的任务，并认为在代码中维护TODO列表不如在错误跟踪系统中高效。
• MaulingMonkey则根据不同情况使用TODO，例如外部问题需要沟通时放在问题跟踪系统，本地更改需要防止错误提交时放在代码注释中。
• basfo和Arainach都认为TODO应指向实际需要完成的任务，而不是仅仅作为注释，以避免责任推卸和混淆。
• indoordin0saur和ngruhn支持使用TODO来记录边缘情况或未来可能的改进，认为它们对未来维护有帮助。
• allthedatas使用分层策略，FIXME用于需要修复的问题，TODO用于可能不那么具体的未来想法。
• joaomeloplus则尽量避免使用注释，认为代码应自解释，只有在非常必要时才使用注释。
• kstrauser强烈反对将TODO作为笔记和行动项混用的做法，认为应明确区分以减少不必要的认知负担。

补充讨论：
• TODO的定义和使用场景在不同开发者和团队中存在较大差异，主要争议在于TODO是否应总是指向具体可执行的任务。
• 一些开发者强调TODO应与问题跟踪系统结合使用以确保任务可跟踪，而另一些开发者则认为TODO作为代码中的注释有其独特价值。
• 讨论中还涉及到不同类型的注释（如FIXME、XXX、NOTE）以区分不同优先级和类型的任务或问题。
• 对于TODO是否导致责任推卸和代码质量下降也存在不同看法，一些开发者认为这取决于团队文化和具体使用方式。
• 工具和流程的有效性也被提及，如何在实际开发中平衡低摩擦捕捉和技术债务管理是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

44646801.article_content:
TODOs aren’t for doing
July 21, 2025
Some teams require that every TODO comment in a codebase gets logged in the bug tracker. Others automatically delete any “stale” TODO that has been in the codebase for over a year. Don’t do it!
TODO comments don’t need to get done in order to be valuable. If you have
// TODO: Write the second half of this file so next week's launch won't explode
then sure, you should probably track that somewhere.
But to me, a good TODO looks more like this:
// TODO: If the user triple-clicks this button, the click handler errors because [xyz]
Would this be the highest-priority thing on the backlog? Probably not. Most users won’t end up triple-clicking that button. But the
// TODO:
doesn’t need to be a plan to actually do something. Instead, it’s a note about “here’s an edge case that wasn’t handled” or a suggestion for a better structure that the author didn’t make time to implement — it captures a little slice of the author’s brain and gives a little window into the rich context they had at the time they wrote the code.
Sometimes TODOs are useful, sometimes they’re not, but well-placed TODOs can often answer a future reader’s “Am I totally missing something, or wouldn’t it better if this code was refactored like this?” — and answer it well enough to get past the hump of “Ehh, maybe I’ll just leave it the way it was in case the original author knew something I don’t.”
44646801.article_summary: 本文讨论了代码中的TODO注释的价值，认为它们不一定要被完成。TODO注释可以是关于未处理的边缘情况或代码结构改进的建议，帮助未来的开发者理解原作者当时的思路和背景，而不必强制将每个TODO都记录到错误跟踪系统或删除过期的注释。例如，针对特定按钮三次点击问题的不处理说明，虽然不是高优先级任务，但为未来可能的改进提供了有价值的参考。TODO注释的主要作用是为代码提供额外背景信息，帮助解决未来读者的疑惑，而非必须执行的任务列表。
